Create opencontractserver/annotations/migrations/0082_seed_authority_namespaces.py:

"""Seed AuthorityNamespace from the static AUTHORITY_PREFIX registry.

Reproduces today's in-code alias map as queryable rows so the registry is
extensible without a code change. Idempotent on re-run via update_or_create.
"""
from django.db import migrations


def seed(apps, schema_editor):
    from opencontractserver.enrichment import constants as C

    AuthorityNamespace = apps.get_model("annotations", "AuthorityNamespace")

    # Collect aliases per prefix from the reverse of AUTHORITY_PREFIX.
    aliases_by_prefix: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for alias, prefix in C.AUTHORITY_PREFIX.items():
        aliases_by_prefix.setdefault(prefix, []).append(alias.lower())

    prefixes = set(C.AUTHORITY_PREFIX.values()) | {C.SEC_RULE_PREFIX}
    for prefix in prefixes:
        jur, typ = C.PREFIX_CLASSIFICATION[prefix]
        AuthorityNamespace.objects.update_or_create(
            prefix=prefix,
            defaults={
                "display_name": C.PREFIX_DISPLAY_NAME[prefix],
                "jurisdiction": jur,
                "authority_type": typ,
                "aliases": sorted(set(aliases_by_prefix.get(prefix, []))),
                "is_global": True,
            },
        )


def unseed(apps, schema_editor):
    from opencontractserver.enrichment import constants as C

    AuthorityNamespace = apps.get_model("annotations", "AuthorityNamespace")
    prefixes = set(C.AUTHORITY_PREFIX.values()) | {C.SEC_RULE_PREFIX}
    AuthorityNamespace.objects.filter(prefix__in=prefixes).delete()


class Migration(migrations.Migration):

    dependencies = [
        ("annotations", "0081_authoritynamespace"),
    ]

    operations = [migrations.RunPython(seed, unseed)]

"""Classify existing CorpusReference law rows by their canonical_key prefix.

Idempotent and forward-only in effect (reverse is a no-op): only rows still
missing a jurisdiction are touched, so re-running never clobbers values a later
detection pass set.
"""
from django.db import migrations


def backfill(apps, schema_editor):
    from opencontractserver.enrichment import constants as C

    CorpusReference = apps.get_model("annotations", "CorpusReference")
    qs = CorpusReference.objects.filter(
        reference_type=C.REF_LAW, jurisdiction__isnull=True
    ).exclude(canonical_key__isnull=True)
    for ref in qs.iterator():
        prefix = (ref.canonical_key or "").split(":", 1)[0]
        classification = C.PREFIX_CLASSIFICATION.get(prefix)
        if classification is None:
            continue
        ref.jurisdiction, ref.authority_type = classification
        ref.save(update_fields=["jurisdiction", "authority_type"])


def noop(apps, schema_editor):
    # Reverse intentionally does nothing: classification is additive metadata.
    pass


class Migration(migrations.Migration):

    dependencies = [
        ("annotations", "0082_seed_authority_namespaces"),
    ]

    operations = [migrations.RunPython(backfill, noop)]

Create opencontractserver/enrichment/abbreviations.py:

"""Citation abbreviation → (prefix, jurisdiction, authority_type) lookup tables.

Public, factual abbreviation data (jurisdiction + code names) — not protected
expression. Extending coverage is a data edit here, never a grammar change.
Keys are the abbreviation EXACTLY as it appears in text; the grammar matcher
escapes them and matches longest-first.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from opencontractserver.enrichment import constants as C

# State statutory codes. prefix is the canonical_key namespace; jurisdiction is
# the hierarchical region code; type is the authority type.
STATE_CODE_ABBREVIATIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]] = {
    "Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code": ("tx-boc", "us-tx", C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_STATUTE),
    "Cal. Corp. Code": ("ca-corp", "us-ca", C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_STATUTE),
    "Cal. Lab. Code": ("ca-lab", "us-ca", C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_STATUTE),
    "N.Y. Bus. Corp. Law": ("ny-bcl", "us-ny", C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_STATUTE),
    "N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law": ("ny-gbl", "us-ny", C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_STATUTE),
    # "Del. Code Ann. tit. 8" IS the DGCL — reuse the existing prefix so the

  • Step 3: Create the federal grammars

Create opencontractserver/enrichment/grammars.py:

"""Tier-2a: generic citation-SHAPE grammars (open-vocabulary detection).

These recognise citation *form* without knowing the body of law, so they catch
authorities outside the registry (state codes, CFR titles, obscure agencies).
Lower precedence than the Tier-1 registry extractor — see reconcile.py. No DB
access; pure functions over text returning Candidate spans.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterator

from opencontractserver.enrichment import constants as C
from opencontractserver.enrichment.abbreviations import STATE_CODE_ABBREVIATIONS
from opencontractserver.enrichment.extractor import Candidate

# Confidence by grammar family — structured numeric cites are high precision;
# bare-Act detection (Task 11) is intentionally lower.
_CONF_STRUCTURED = 0.9

# A section token: digits, optional trailing letter, optional (a)(2) subsections,
# optional hyphenated rule tail (10b-5, 261.4).
_SEC = r"\d+[A-Za-z]?(?:\.\d+)?(?:[-–]\d+)?(?:\([0-9a-zA-Z]+\))*"

_USC_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?P<title>\d+)\s+U\.?\s?S\.?\s?C\.?\s+(?:§+\s*)?(?P<sec>" + _SEC + r")"
)
_CFR_RE = re.compile(
    r"\b(?P<title>\d+)\s+C\.?\s?F\.?\s?R\.?\s+(?:§+\s*)?(?P<sec>\d+\.\d+"
    r"(?:[-–]\d+)?(?:\([0-9a-zA-Z]+\))*)"
)
_FEDREG_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?P<vol>\d+)\s+Fed\.?\s?Reg\.?\s+(?P<page>\d[\d,]*)")
_PUBL_RE = re.compile(
    r"\bPub(?:lic)?\.?\s?L(?:aw)?\.?\s?No\.?\s?(?P<cong>\d+)[-–](?P<num>\d+)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)
_STAT_RE = re.compile(r"\b(?P<vol>\d+)\s+Stat\.?\s+(?P<page>\d[\d,]*)")


def _cand(start, end, raw, key, jur, typ, conf=_CONF_STRUCTURED) -> Candidate:
    return Candidate(
        reference_type=C.REF_LAW,
        start=start,
        end=end,
        raw_text=raw,
        canonical_key=key,
        normalized_data={"authority": key.split(":", 1)[0], "tier": "grammar"},
        jurisdiction=jur,
        authority_type=typ,
        detection_tier=C.DETECTION_TIER_GRAMMAR,
        detection_confidence=conf,
    )


def _usc(text: str) -> Iterator[Candidate]:
    for m in _USC_RE.finditer(text):
        key = f"usc-{m.group('title')}:{m.group('sec').lower()}"
        yield _cand(
            m.start(), m.end(), m.group(0), key,
            C.JURISDICTION_US_FEDERAL, C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_STATUTE,
        )


def _cfr(text: str) -> Iterator[Candidate]:
    for m in _CFR_RE.finditer(text):
        key = f"cfr-{m.group('title')}:{m.group('sec').lower()}"
        yield _cand(
            m.start(), m.end(), m.group(0), key,
            C.JURISDICTION_US_FEDERAL, C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_REGULATION,
        )


def _fedreg(text: str) -> Iterator[Candidate]:
    for m in _FEDREG_RE.finditer(text):
        page = m.group("page").replace(",", "")
        key = f"fedreg:{m.group('vol')}.{page}"
        yield _cand(
            m.start(), m.end(), m.group(0), key,
            C.JURISDICTION_US_FEDERAL, C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_ADMIN_RULE,
        )


def _publ(text: str) -> Iterator[Candidate]:
    for m in _PUBL_RE.finditer(text):
        key = f"publ:{m.group('cong')}-{m.group('num')}"
        yield _cand(
            m.start(), m.end(), m.group(0), key,
            C.JURISDICTION_US_FEDERAL, C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_STATUTE,
        )


def _stat(text: str) -> Iterator[Candidate]:
    for m in _STAT_RE.finditer(text):
        page = m.group("page").replace(",", "")
        key = f"stat:{m.group('vol')}.{page}"
        yield _cand(
            m.start(), m.end(), m.group(0), key,
            C.JURISDICTION_US_FEDERAL, C.AUTHORITY_TYPE_STATUTE,
        )


class GenericCitationExtractor:
    """Run all Tier-2a shape grammars over text → list[Candidate]."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        # State-code alternation, longest-first so "Del. Code Ann. tit. 8" wins
        # over a hypothetical "Del. Code". Compiled once per instance.
        ordered = sorted(STATE_CODE_ABBREVIATIONS, key=len, reverse=True)
        self._state_alt = "|".join(re.escape(a) for a in ordered)
        self._state_re = (
            re.compile(
                r"(?P<abbr>" + self._state_alt + r")\s+(?:§+\s*)?(?P<sec>"
                + _SEC + r")"
            )
            if ordered
            else None
        )

    def extract(self, text: str) -> list[Candidate]:
        out: list[Candidate] = []
        out.extend(_usc(text))
        out.extend(_cfr(text))
        out.extend(_fedreg(text))
        out.extend(_publ(text))
        out.extend(_stat(text))
        out.extend(self._states(text))
        return out

    def _states(self, text: str) -> Iterator[Candidate]:
        if self._state_re is None:
            return
        for m in self._state_re.finditer(text):
            prefix, jur, typ = STATE_CODE_ABBREVIATIONS[m.group("abbr")]
            key = f"{prefix}:{m.group('sec').lower()}"
            yield _cand(m.start(), m.end(), m.group(0), key, jur, typ)

  • Step 3: Create reconcile

Create opencontractserver/enrichment/reconcile.py:

"""Merge detection layers with precedence: registry > grammar > llm.

A higher-precedence candidate suppresses any lower or equal-precedence
candidate whose span overlaps it. Within a single layer, the earlier span (by
start offset) wins an overlap. The Tier-1 (registry) list is always preserved
in full — callers pass it as ``primary``.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from opencontractserver.enrichment.extractor import Candidate


def _overlaps(a: tuple[int, int], b: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
    return not (a[1] <= b[0] or a[0] >= b[1])


def reconcile(
    primary: list[Candidate], secondary: list[Candidate]
) -> list[Candidate]:
    """Keep all ``primary``; add ``secondary`` candidates that don't overlap a
    kept span. ``secondary`` is processed in document order so the earliest
    span wins an intra-layer overlap."""
    kept: list[Candidate] = list(primary)
    occupied: list[tuple[int, int]] = [(c.start, c.end) for c in primary]
    for cand in sorted(secondary, key=lambda c: (c.start, c.end)):
        span = (cand.start, cand.end)
        if any(_overlaps(span, used) for used in occupied):
            continue
        kept.append(cand)
        occupied.append(span)
    return kept

"""Open-vocabulary discovery surfaces non-registry authorities."""

_TEXT = (

    "40 C.F.R. § 261.4. It is also governed by Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code § 21.401 "
    "and Section 145 of the Delaware General Corporation Law."

class DiscoveryTests(TestCase):

        self.doc.txt_extract_file.save("d.txt", ContentFile(_TEXT.encode()))

            corpus_id=self.corpus.id, creator_id=self.user.id
        )

        assert "usc-15:78j(b)" not in keys  # not detected at registry tier

    def test_grammar_tier_finds_open_vocabulary_authorities(self):

            corpus_id=self.corpus.id, creator_id=self.user.id
        )
        keys = set(out["by_key"])
        assert "usc-15:78j(b)" in keys
        assert "cfr-40:261.4" in keys
        assert "tx-boc:21.401" in keys
        # Grouped by jurisdiction.
        assert "us-tx" in out["by_jurisdiction"]
        # The Texas code is NOT in the namespace registry → flagged as new.
        assert any(n["prefix"] == "tx-boc" for n in out["new_namespaces"])

    def _resolutions(
        self, corpus, documents, types, user, tiers=None
    ) -> list[Resolution]:
        from opencontractserver.enrichment.authorities import authority_alias_registry
        from opencontractserver.enrichment.grammars import GenericCitationExtractor
        from opencontractserver.enrichment.reconcile import reconcile

        wanted = set(types or C.DEFAULT_REFERENCE_TYPES)
        active_tiers = set(tiers or (C.DETECTION_TIER_REGISTRY,))
        resolver = ReferenceResolver(documents)
        extractor = ReferenceExtractor(authority_aliases=authority_alias_registry(user))
        generic = (
            GenericCitationExtractor()
            if C.DETECTION_TIER_GRAMMAR in active_tiers
            else None
        )
        sections_by_doc = self._sections_by_doc(documents)
        resolutions: list[Resolution] = []
        for doc in documents:
            try:
                text = read_field_file_text(doc.txt_extract_file)
            except Exception as exc:  # isolate per-document failures
                logger.warning(
                    "Enrichment: skip doc %s (text read failed: %s)", doc.id, exc
                )
                continue
            if not text:
                continue
            sections = sections_by_doc.get(doc.id, [])
            meta = doc.custom_meta if isinstance(doc.custom_meta, dict) else {}
            primary = list(
                extractor.extract(text, default_authority=meta.get("authority"))
            )
            if generic is not None:
                # Registry wins on overlap; generic adds the open-vocabulary tail.
                cands = reconcile(primary, generic.extract(text))
            else:
                cands = primary
            for cand in cands:
                if cand.reference_type not in wanted:
                    continue
                resolutions.append(resolver.resolve(cand, doc.id, text, sections))
        return resolutions

Append a new method to EnrichmentService (after scan, before get_analyzer):

    def discover(
        self,
        *,
        corpus_id: int,
        creator_id: int,
    ) -> dict:
        """Read-only open-vocabulary inventory (registry + grammar tiers).

        Surfaces authorities the registry alone would miss, grouped by
        jurisdiction / authority_type, and flags prefixes with no
        AuthorityNamespace row (genuinely new bodies of law).
        """
        from collections import Counter

        from opencontractserver.annotations.models import AuthorityNamespace

        user, corpus, documents = self._load(corpus_id, creator_id)
        resolutions = self._resolutions(
            corpus,
            documents,
            [C.REF_LAW],
            user,
            tiers=[C.DETECTION_TIER_REGISTRY, C.DETECTION_TIER_GRAMMAR],
        )

        by_key: dict[str, dict] = {}
        by_jurisdiction: Counter = Counter()
        by_type: Counter = Counter()
        prefixes: set[str] = set()
        for r in resolutions:
            key = r.canonical_key
            if not key:
                continue
            cand = r.candidate
            prefix = key.split(":", 1)[0]
            prefixes.add(prefix)
            entry = by_key.setdefault(
                key,
                {
                    "canonical_key": key,
                    "prefix": prefix,
                    "jurisdiction": cand.jurisdiction,
                    "authority_type": cand.authority_type,
                    "detection_tier": cand.detection_tier,
                    "mention_count": 0,
                },
            )
            entry["mention_count"] += 1
            if cand.jurisdiction:
                by_jurisdiction[cand.jurisdiction] += 1
            if cand.authority_type:
                by_type[cand.authority_type] += 1

        known = set(
            AuthorityNamespace.objects.filter(prefix__in=prefixes).values_list(
                "prefix", flat=True
            )
        )
        new_namespaces = [
            {"prefix": p, "jurisdiction": None, "authority_type": None}
            for p in sorted(prefixes - known)
        ]
        # Enrich new-namespace classification from any detected key for that prefix.
        prefix_class = {
            e["prefix"]: (e["jurisdiction"], e["authority_type"])
            for e in by_key.values()
        }
        for n in new_namespaces:
            n["jurisdiction"], n["authority_type"] = prefix_class.get(
                n["prefix"], (None, None)
            )

        return {
            "corpus_id": corpus_id,
            "documents_scanned": len(documents),
            "total_candidates": len(resolutions),
            "by_key": by_key,
            "by_jurisdiction": dict(by_jurisdiction),
            "by_authority_type": dict(by_type),
            "new_namespaces": new_namespaces,
        }

def discover_authorities(
    *,

    creator_id: int,

    """Open-vocabulary authority inventory (read-only).

Spec coverage (Phases 0 + 1 of 2026-06-14-...-design.md):

  • Component 1 (jurisdiction/authority_type taxonomy) → Tasks 1, 2, 6. ✔
  • Component 1 (AuthorityNamespace registry + alias-registry read) → Tasks 3, 4, 5. ✔
  • Component 1 (equivalence table) → deferred to Phase ¾ per spec §15 (Del. Code→dgcl prefix mapping in Task 8 gives partial dedup now). ✔ (intentional)
  • Component 2 Tier 1 (registry unchanged) → preserved; Task 7 asserts detection_tier="registry". ✔
  • Component 2 Tier 2a (generic grammars: USC/CFR/FedReg/PubL/Stat/state/municipal/bare-Act) → Tasks 9, 10, 11. Municipal: a generic municipal pattern is not in Tasks 9–11; see gap note below.
  • Component 2 reconciliation → Task 12. ✔

  • Detection provenance columns → Tasks 13, 14. ✔
  • Surfaces: discover_authorities tool + discover() → Tasks 15, 16. GraphQL/governance-graph regime coloring → Phase 5 per spec §15. ✔ (intentional)

Gap found & resolved: the spec's §5.2 table lists a municipal form (S.F. Police Code art. 38), but Tasks 9–11 ship only federal + state + bare-Act grammars. Municipal citation shapes are highly heterogeneous; rather than a half-built municipal regex, municipal detection is explicitly deferred to a Phase-1 follow-up task (add a generic <Place> Municipal Code § N grammar + MUNICIPAL_ABBREVIATIONS table) tracked as its own issue. This keeps Phase 1's state/federal coverage solid and honest rather than shipping a municipal matcher with poor precision. Flagged here so it is not silently dropped.

Placeholder scan: no TBD/TODO/"handle appropriately"; every code step shows complete code; every test shows real assertions. ✔

GenericCitationExtractor().extract() defined in Task 9 matches usage in Tasks 10, 11, 15. discover() return shape (by_key, by_jurisdiction, new_namespaces) defined in Task 15 matches assertions in Tasks 15, 16. ✔

Migration chain: 0080 → 0081 → 0082 → 0083 (Phase 0) → 0084 (Phase 1), each declaring the prior as a dependency. ✔ ```

    corpus=corpus, annotation_label__text=C.LABEL_IMPACT,
    data__event_id=event.id, document_id__in=visible_ids,

rows, auth, ent = [], Counter(), Counter()
for a in anns:
    d = a.data or {}
    rows.append({"document_id": a.document_id, "title": str(a.document.title),
                 "score": d.get("impact_score", 0.0),
                 "authority_matches": d.get("authority_matches", []),
                 "entity_matches": d.get("entity_matches", []),
                 "semantic_score": d.get("semantic_score", 0.0)})
    auth.update(d.get("authority_matches", [])); ent.update(d.get("entity_matches", []))
rows.sort(key=lambda r: r["score"], reverse=True)
dominant = "authority" if auth else ("entity" if ent else ("semantic" if rows else None))
# run_status: latest impact Analysis for this corpus still RUNNING?

    analyzed_corpus=corpus, analyzer__task_name=C.IMPACT_ANALYZER_TASK,
    status="RUNNING").exists()
return {"documents_impacted": len(rows), "dominant_signal": dominant,
        "top_authorities": [k for k, _ in auth.most_common(5)],
        "top_entities": [k for k, _ in ent.most_common(5)],

docs.title: Design: Stop sending empty Authorization header from Apollo (issue #1431)
Design: Stop sending empty Authorization header from Apollo (issue #1431)
docs.text: Date: 2026-05-01 Issue: #1431 Follow-up: #1432 — backend CSRF hardening (out of scope here) Branch: claude/fix-empty-auth-header-1431

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
Production logs show a steady stream of 403 Forbidden (CSRF token missing.) on POST /graphql/. Root cause is purely client-side: frontend/src/index.tsx always sets Authorization: token ? "Bearer …" : "", and the backend's conditional_csrf_exempt (config/graphql/security.py:43) treats the empty string as falsy and falls into the session+CSRF branch. The SPA has no CSRF flow (Bearer-only by design), so the request 403s.

This spec fixes the frontend at the Apollo transport layer and removes a related noisy log in Auth0JWTSettings.__getattr__. Broader backend hardening is tracked separately in #1432.

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
1. Empty Authorization: when authToken() returns "" (Auth0 still loading, refresh failed, expired token, logged out), the Authorization header is sent as "". The backend's session/CSRF path rejects every such request.
  2. Startup race: <ApolloProvider> is mounted above <AuthGate> in frontend/src/index.tsx. AuthGate gates child rendering until Auth0 finishes, but Apollo itself is alive earlier. Any code path that issues a query during the gating window reaches the network without a token.
  3. Log noise: Auth0JWTSettings.__getattr__ (config/graphql_auth0_auth/settings.py:73-79) logs unknown-attribute access at ERROR. Python uses unknown-attr probes routinely (hasattr, pickle, deepcopy, _user_settings lookup, dunder methods); these are normal AttributeError control flow, not errors.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• No Authorization: "" ever leaves the SPA.
  • No GraphQL operation reaches the network before AuthGate has resolved auth state (token or anonymous).
  • Mid-session token expiry behavior unchanged (errorLink already handles 401/403 → reload → AuthGate re-run).
  • Auth0JWTSettings no longer ERROR-logs normal AttributeError flow.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Adding CSRF token plumbing to the SPA (it remains Bearer-only).
  • Modifying conditional_csrf_exempt semantics — see #1432.
  • Changing AuthGate's UX choices around refresh failure (still falls back to anonymous).
  • Forcing redirect-to-login on token absence (existing UX is anonymous browsing).

docs.title: Approach
docs.text:
Replace the synchronous ApolloLink in frontend/src/index.tsx with a setContext-based async link that:

  1. Awaits authInitCompleteVar before computing headers, using onNextChange (event-driven, not polled).
  2. Conditionally spreads Authorization: Bearer <token> only when authToken() is non-empty.

Extract the link into its own module so it can be unit-tested in isolation.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Caller (component / hook)
        │
        ▼
ApolloClient.query / mutate
        │
        ▼
errorLink ── setContext(authLink) ── httpLink ──► /graphql/
              │
              ├─ if !authInitCompleteVar(): await onNextChange(true)
              ├─ token = authToken()
              └─ headers = { ...headers, ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}) }

Single choke point — every operation passes through authLink. AuthGate continues to gate React rendering for a smooth UX; the link gates the transport for correctness.

docs.title: 1. frontend/src/graphql/authLink.ts (new)
docs.text:
import { setContext } from "@apollo/client/link/context";
import { authToken, authInitCompleteVar } from "./cache";

/**
 * Resolves once auth initialization has completed (token resolved or anonymous).
 * Uses Apollo's reactive-var onNextChange so the wait is event-driven.
 */
export function waitForAuthInit(): Promise<void> {
  if (authInitCompleteVar()) return Promise.resolve();
  return new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    const unsubscribe = authInitCompleteVar.onNextChange((value) => {
      if (value) {
        unsubscribe();
        resolve();
      }
    });
  });
}

/**
 * Apollo auth link.
 *
 * Defers operations until AuthGate has finished initializing, then attaches
 * a Bearer token if one is available. Sending an empty Authorization header
 * trips the backend's conditional CSRF check and produces 403s, so we omit
 * the header entirely when no token is present.
 */
export const authLink = setContext(async (_operation, { headers }) => {
  await waitForAuthInit();
  const token = authToken();
  return {
    headers: {
      ...headers,
      ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}),
    },
  };
});

In Auth0JWTSettings.__getattr__, drop the logger.error(...) line. The raise AttributeError(...) stays. The DEBUG log at the top of the method also stays — it's useful for diagnostics and only fires at DEBUG level.

Before:

After:

    if attr not in self.defaults:
        raise AttributeError(f"Invalid setting: `{attr}`")
    ...

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
Authenticated user, app boot (Auth0): 1. <ApolloProvider> mounts; authInitCompleteVar is false. 2. Component fires a query → setContext runs → awaits onNextChange. 3. <AuthGate> calls getAccessTokenSilently(), sets authToken(token), sets authInitCompleteVar(true). 4. setContext resolves, attaches Authorization: Bearer <token>, request goes to /graphql/.

Anonymous user (Auth0, no session): 1. Same as above through step 2. 2. AuthGate's silent-token call fails → sets authToken(""), authInitCompleteVar(true). 3. setContext resolves, omits Authorization, request goes to /graphql/ as anonymous. Public queries succeed; protected ones get a clean auth error handled by errorLink.

Non-Auth0 mode: 1. <AuthGate> immediately sets authInitCompleteVar(true) (AuthGate.tsx:92-101). 2. setContext resolves immediately on every operation. If a Bearer token has been set via the login form, it's attached; otherwise the request is anonymous.

Mid-session token expiry: Unchanged. Stale Bearer goes out, backend returns 401/403, errorLink reloads the page, AuthGate re-runs.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text: Scenario Behavior AuthGate hangs forever getAccessTokenSilently has a 10s timeout (AuthGate.tsx:279); on timeout AuthGate flips authInitCompleteVar(true) with empty token. Link unblocks. onNextChange never fires Cannot happen given the above timeout, but worst case the user sees a hung query — same UX as today's race. No regression. Token expires after init Stale header sent → backend 401/403 → errorLink reloads → AuthGate refreshes. Existing flow. User logs out authToken("") set synchronously; next operation omits Authorization and is treated as anonymous. Apollo cache reads (no network) Don't traverse the link. Unaffected.

docs.title: New unit tests — frontend/src/graphql/authLink.test.ts (Vitest)
docs.text:
Drive the link with execute() from @apollo/client/core composed with a terminating ApolloLink stub that captures the operation's headers. Manipulate authToken / authInitCompleteVar directly (they're exported from cache.ts).

  1. Empty token, init complete → terminating link sees no Authorization key in headers.
  2. Valid token, init complete → terminating link sees Authorization: Bearer <token>.
  3. Init not complete → terminating link is not invoked; after authInitCompleteVar(true), it is invoked with correct headers.
  4. Token set but init not complete → still gated on init flag (proves the gate is on init completion, not token presence).
  5. waitForAuthInit() resolves synchronously when init is already complete (guards against subscription leaks).

  4. Tail docker compose -f local.yml logs django and confirm Forbidden (CSRF token missing.) no longer fires during normal browsing.

docs.title: Rollout
docs.text:
• Single PR targeting main.
  • No migrations.
  • No env-var changes.
  • No feature flag — fix is strictly safer than current behavior.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• onNextChange semantics: Apollo's reactive-var subscription fires on the next change, not the current value. The waitForAuthInit() helper checks the current value first to avoid waiting forever if init completed before the subscription was set up. This is covered by test case 5.
  • @apollo/client/link/context: standard Apollo subpackage; already a transitive dep of @apollo/client. No new package install.
  • Behavior in tests that mount components without AuthGate: existing test wrappers set authInitCompleteVar(true) (or its equivalent) — verify a couple of representative wrappers still set this var. If any wrapper relies on the old synchronous link behavior (operations firing before init), it will hang. Mitigation: a quick grep + spot-check during implementation; if anything breaks, the fix is one line in the wrapper.

docs.title: Out of scope
docs.text:
• Backend hardening of conditional_csrf_exempt (#1432).
  • Migrating <ApolloProvider> below <AuthGate> in the React tree. Theoretically tidier but invasive — the link-level gate achieves the same outcome with much less surgery.
  • Refresh-token-from-link logic. Duplicates AuthGate; conflicts with the existing "fall back to anonymous" UX.

docs.title: WebSocket Auth Handshake — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-05-03 Branch: feature/websocket-auth-handshake Status: Approved (brainstorming complete; awaiting implementation plan)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Today, the frontend authenticates WebSocket connections by appending a JWT to the URL query string (ws://.../ws/agent-chat/?token=<jwt>). The backend's JWTAuthMiddleware extracts that token and validates it via config/jwt_utils.get_user_from_jwt_token. This is correct functionally but leaks tokens through every system that records request URLs:

  • Reverse-proxy access logs (nginx, Daphne)
  • Browser history and Referer headers
  • Sentry breadcrumbs and other monitoring
  • CDN / WAF logs

Token rotation also requires a full disconnect + reconnect, which churns subscriptions, drops in-flight agent streams, and races refresh against re-auth.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. Move JWT off the URL entirely. Initial transport is the standard Sec-WebSocket-Protocol handshake header — the only auth-bearing channel a browser WebSocket constructor can populate.
  2. Provide an in-band AUTH message protocol so token rotation does not require reconnect.
  3. Preserve every existing per-consumer access policy (anonymous-allowed for public docs, auth-required for thread/notification streams).
  4. Make user-pk swap on a live socket impossible (defense in depth).
  5. Make resource-permission revocation observable mid-connection (refresh re-validates).
  6. Test the system thoroughly: middleware, mixin, three consumers, three frontend hooks, and regression coverage for the leaks this fix prevents.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Changing REST/GraphQL auth (covered by rest_jwt_auth.py and Auth0 GraphQL middleware).
  • Changing how Auth0 vs. graphql_jwt is selected (USE_AUTH0 switch in jwt_utils.py is unchanged).
  • Maintaining backwards compatibility with the old ?token= transport — this is a hard cutover (see §11).

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: # Decision Rationale 1 Hybrid transport — subprotocol for initial token, in-band AUTH message for refresh Preserves connect-time permission checks; refresh without reconnect 2 Per-consumer anonymous policy unchanged Three consumers have intentionally different access models; only transport changes 3 Both client-driven and server-nudged refresh Client covers happy path (Auth0 silent renewal); server covers idle / missed-rotation edge case 4 Both auth backends (Auth0 + graphql_jwt) jwt_utils already abstracts; no fork needed 5 All three frontend hooks updated; deprecated wrappers deleted No dead code per CLAUDE.md 6 Hard cutover — old ?token= transport stripped Old transport is the bug; dual-accept defeats the purpose 7 Subprotocol format ["opencontracts.jwt.v1", "<token>"] Server echoes only the marker, not the token 8 Mutate scope["user"] post-handshake Lower-risk; existing readers unchanged 9 On refresh: identity + permissions + close-on-pk-mismatch Refresh must never become a user-swap backdoor 10 Backend + frontend hook unit tests; no Playwright CT in v1 CT is expensive to maintain; jsdom is sufficient

docs.text:

│  │    jwt_utils.get_user_from_jwt_token                             │   │
│  │  • Sets scope["user"], scope["auth_error"],                      │   │
│  │    scope["accepted_subprotocol"] = "opencontracts.jwt.v1"        │   │
│  │  • Does NOT read query string for token (security fix)           │   │
│  │  • Does NOT read Authorization header (browsers can't set it)    │   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│        │                                                                │
│        ▼                                                                │
│  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │
│  │ AuthHandshakeMixin (new) — added to all 3 consumer base classes  │   │
│  │  • accept_with_auth() echoes accepted_subprotocol                │   │
│  │  • handle_auth_message() re-validates token, swaps scope.user,   │   │
│  │    refuses pk swap (4002), refuses revoked perms (4003)          │   │
│  │  • nudge_refresh_if_expired() emits AUTH_REFRESH_REQUIRED        │   │
│  │    with grace-timer that closes 4001 on timeout                  │   │
│  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │
│        │                                                                │
│        ▼                                                                │
│  UnifiedAgentConsumer / NotificationUpdatesConsumer /                   │
│  ThreadUpdatesConsumer — unchanged business logic; consume the mixin   │
│  and route AUTH messages first in receive().                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Backend
docs.text: File Change Purpose config/websocket/middleware.py Rewrite JWTAuthMiddleware Drop query-string + Authorization-header extraction; read token only from Sec-WebSocket-Protocol. Set scope["accepted_subprotocol"]. Keep close-code constants; add WS_AUTH_SUBPROTOCOL = "opencontracts.jwt.v1". config/websocket/auth_handshake.py New AuthHandshakeMixin accept_with_auth() calls self.accept(subprotocol=self.scope.get("accepted_subprotocol")). handle_auth_message(payload) → re-validate, refuse user-pk swap (4002), refuse if user lacks permission on currently-bound resources (4003), reply AUTH_OK / AUTH_FAILED. nudge_refresh_if_expired() → emit AUTH_REFRESH_REQUIRED and start a 30s grace timer that closes 4001 on timeout. Exposes current_user mirroring scope["user"]. config/websocket/utils/auth_helpers.py Verify No semantic change; ensure compatibility with new middleware. config/websocket/consumers/unified_agent_conversation.py Update Inherit AuthHandshakeMixin; replace await self.accept() with await self.accept_with_auth(); in receive(), route type == "AUTH" before JSON-payload dispatch; factor existing connect-time permission checks into reusable _validate_resource_permissions(user) so refresh re-runs them. config/websocket/consumers/notification_updates.py Update Same mixin integration. User-pk swap is forbidden by mixin, so notification_user_{pk} group remains valid. config/websocket/consumers/thread_updates.py Update Same mixin integration. docs.title: Not changing
docs.text:
• jwt_utils.py — already the unified validation entry point.
  • rest_jwt_auth.py — REST/HTTP unaffected.
  • The 3 consumers' business logic (streaming, approvals, permissions).
  • Auth0 user-creation logic — still triggered through get_user_from_jwt_token.

docs.title: Initial connection (authenticated)
docs.text:
Client                                      Server (middleware)              Consumer
  │                                                 │                            │
  │ ws = new WebSocket(url, [                       │                            │
  │   "opencontracts.jwt.v1", "<jwt>"               │                            │
  │ ])                                              │                            │
  │ ─── HTTP UPGRADE ──────────────────────────────►│                            │
  │     Sec-WebSocket-Protocol:                     │                            │
  │       opencontracts.jwt.v1, <jwt>               │                            │
  │                                                 │ Validate <jwt> via         │
  │                                                 │ jwt_utils.get_user_…       │
  │                                                 │ scope["user"] = User       │
  │                                                 │ scope["accepted_subprot…"] │
  │                                                 │   = "opencontracts.jwt.v1" │
  │                                                 │ ───────────────────────────►│
  │                                                 │                            │ accept_with_auth()
  │ ◄──── 101 Switching Protocols ──────────────────┼────────────────────────────┤
  │       Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: opencontracts.jwt.v1                           │
  │                                                                              │
  │ ◄── {"type":"AUTH_OK","user_id":123,"username":"alice"}  ────────────────────│

docs.title: Initial connection (anonymous, no token)
docs.text:
ws = new WebSocket(url, ["opencontracts.jwt.v1"])
  → middleware: no token in subprotocol → AnonymousUser, no auth_error
  → consumer: per-policy decision (close 4000 if auth required, else continue)
  → if accepted: server sends {"type":"AUTH_OK","user_id":null,"anonymous":true}

docs.title: Initial connection (invalid token)
docs.text:
ws = new WebSocket(url, ["opencontracts.jwt.v1", "<garbage>"])
  → middleware: validation raises JSONWebTokenError
  → scope.user = AnonymousUser, auth_error = {code:4002, message:…}
  → consumer: check_auth_and_close_if_failed() closes 4002
  → client: ws.onclose code 4002 → trigger re-login flow

docs.title: Token refresh — client-driven (happy path)
docs.text:
Client (authToken changes via Auth0 silent renewal / Apollo refresh)
  │
  │ ws.send({"type":"AUTH","token":"<new jwt>"})
  │ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►│
  │                                                               │ handle_auth_message():
  │                                                               │   1. validate token via jwt_utils
  │                                                               │   2. assert new_user.pk == self.current_user.pk
  │                                                               │      (else AUTH_FAILED + close 4002)
  │                                                               │   3. _validate_resource_permissions(new_user)
  │                                                               │      (else AUTH_FAILED + close 4003)
  │                                                               │   4. self.scope["user"] = new_user
  │                                                               │   5. cancel pending refresh-grace-timer
  │                                                               │
  │ ◄── {"type":"AUTH_OK","user_id":123,"refreshed":true}  ───────│
  │
  │ (existing stream / subscription continues uninterrupted)

docs.title: Token refresh — server-nudged
docs.text:
Server detects expired token mid-stream
  │ ◄── {"type":"AUTH_REFRESH_REQUIRED","grace_seconds":30}  ──── starts grace timer
  │
  │ Client (useWebSocketAuth) sees AUTH_REFRESH_REQUIRED:
  │   - if authToken in cache is still the same expired token,
  │     calls Apollo/Auth0 refresh hook
  │   - sends {"type":"AUTH","token":"<new>"}
  │
  │ ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────►│ → AUTH_OK (normal refresh path)
  │
  │ If client doesn't refresh in 30s:
  │ ◄── close 4001 (TOKEN_EXPIRED) ───────────────────────────────│ → client reconnects

docs.title: Refresh failure — user-pk swap (security guard)
docs.text:
Client (somehow): ws.send({"type":"AUTH","token":"<token-for-different-user>"})
  → Server: new_user.pk != self.current_user.pk
  → Server: send {"type":"AUTH_FAILED","reason":"USER_MISMATCH"}
  → Server: close 4002
  → Rationale: a live socket bound to user A must never silently re-bind to user B.

docs.title: Wire protocol
docs.text:
Client → Server 

{"type": "AUTH", "token": "<jwt>"}

Server → Client 

// Initial post-accept handshake confirmation
{"type": "AUTH_OK", "user_id": 123, "username": "alice", "anonymous": false, "refreshed": false}
{"type": "AUTH_OK", "user_id": null, "anonymous": true,  "refreshed": false}

// Refresh succeeded
{"type": "AUTH_OK", "user_id": 123, "refreshed": true}

// Refresh failed (followed by close)
{"type": "AUTH_FAILED", "reason": "EXPIRED" | "INVALID" | "USER_MISMATCH" | "PERMISSION_REVOKED"}

// Server requesting refresh
{"type": "AUTH_REFRESH_REQUIRED", "grace_seconds": 30}

All AUTH_* types use the uppercase AUTH_ prefix to avoid colliding with existing ASYNC_*, SYNC_*, or NOTIFICATION_* consumer messages.

docs.title: Close codes
docs.text: Code Meaning Triggered by 1000 Normal closure Client disconnect() 4000 WS_CLOSE_UNAUTHENTICATED Anonymous user, consumer requires auth 4001 WS_CLOSE_TOKEN_EXPIRED Initial token expired, OR refresh-grace timer expired 4002 WS_CLOSE_TOKEN_INVALID Initial token malformed/invalid, OR refresh attempted user-pk swap 4003 Permission denied Resource permission check fails 4029 WS_CLOSE_RATE_LIMITED Connection throttled

docs.title: Token validation paths
docs.text: Scenario Middleware behavior Consumer behavior Wire result No subprotocol header at all scope.user = AnonymousUser, no auth_error Per-policy: accept or close 4000 If accepted: AUTH_OK anonymous:true Subprotocol present, no token slot scope.user = AnonymousUser, no auth_error Same as above Same Subprotocol present, token expired scope.user = AnonymousUser, auth_error = Closes 4001 Close 4001 Subprotocol present, token invalid scope.user = AnonymousUser, auth_error = Closes 4002 Close 4002 Subprotocol present, valid token, user inactive JSONWebTokenError("User is disabled") → auth_error = Closes 4002 Close 4002

docs.title: Subprotocol negotiation
docs.text:
• Server always echoes a selected subprotocol when one was offered (including the anonymous case ["opencontracts.jwt.v1"]). Otherwise browsers fail the connection.
  • Hard cutover: old client (?token=-only) connects to new server → no subprotocol → AnonymousUser → consumer closes 4000 if auth required. Acceptable per Decision #6.
  • Reverse-proxy note: nginx forwards Sec-WebSocket-Protocol by default. A deployment-time docs update in docs/websocket/auth.md will call this out explicitly.

docs.title: Refresh failure modes
docs.text: Failure Server action Client action AUTH payload missing token field AUTH_FAILED INVALID, close 4002 Reconnect from scratch AUTH payload's token expired AUTH_FAILED EXPIRED, close 4001 Refresh, then reconnect AUTH payload's token invalid AUTH_FAILED INVALID, close 4002 Hard re-login AUTH payload's token belongs to different user AUTH_FAILED USER_MISMATCH, close 4002 Hard re-login AUTH succeeds but resource permission revoked AUTH_FAILED PERMISSION_REVOKED, close 4003 Close gracefully Server-nudge not answered within grace_seconds Close 4001 Reconnect with fresh token

docs.title: Race conditions
docs.text:
1. Token rotates exactly during initial handshake — middleware closes 4001; client reconnects with new token. No special handling.
  2. Multiple AUTH messages in flight — Channels' AsyncWebsocketConsumer.receive is sequential per connection; serial processing.
  3. Stream in flight when refresh arrives — detect AUTH at the top of receive(), dispatch synchronously without entering the agent-query rate-limit gate or _initialize_agent. Pure metadata mutation on scope["user"].
  4. Channel-layer group membership stale after refresh — only relevant if user-pk could change. Forbidden by USER_MISMATCH check; groups remain valid.
  5. Refresh timer fires after disconnect — store timer task on self._refresh_grace_task; cancel in disconnect().
  6. Two browser tabs, one logs out — token reactive var transitions valid→null; useWebSocketAuth must clean-close (1000) and reconnect anonymous, NOT send AUTH with empty token.

docs.title: Frontend reconnection logic
docs.text:
Existing exponential backoff stays. Refinement encapsulated in useWebSocketAuth:

  • 1000 (normal) → no reconnect
  • 4001 (token expired) → trigger token refresh, then reconnect
  • 4002 (token invalid) → reconnect anonymous (or fire onAuthInvalid callback)
  • 4003 (permission denied) → no reconnect
  • 4029 (rate-limited) → reconnect with longer delay
  • 1006 / unknown → existing exponential backoff

docs.title: Sentry / log-leak hygiene
docs.text: After implementation: - Confirm WS URL strings in Sentry breadcrumbs no longer carry ?token=. - Add a Sentry before_send scrub for Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header values (defense in depth). - Confirm Daphne access logs don't include subprotocol header values (default behavior — they don't).

docs.title: PII Scan & Auto-Annotate Tool — Design
docs.text: Status: Draft Date: 2026-05-11 Author: scrudato

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Add an agent tool that scans an OpenContracts document for sensitive information using the privacy-filter microservice and creates one labeled annotation per detection.

  • PDFs → token-level annotations via PlasmaPDF (TOKEN_LABEL).
  • Plain text → character-span annotations (SPAN_LABEL).
  • Both share the agent-tool contract used by add_annotations_from_exact_strings (sync core + a-prefixed async wrapper, requires_approval=True, requires_write_permission=True).

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Auto-trigger on corpus ingest. The tool already accepts corpus_action_id, so wiring is a one-liner later but is not part of this spec.
  • Redaction/anonymization (replacing PII with placeholders).
  • A separate "scan a raw text snippet" tool (no document_id). Trivial to add later by exposing the chunker directly.
  • Dedicated PII-only UI; existing annotation chrome handles labels and filters.

docs.title: External Dependency: privacy-filter
docs.text:
A stateless FastAPI service with one production endpoint:

  • POST /v1/detect, X-API-Key header, JSON {"text": "..."}.
  • Response: {"detections": [{"entity_group", "score", "word", "start", "end"}, ...]}.
  • /healthz (liveness) and /readyz (503 until model loaded).
  • Default MAX_INPUT_CHARS = 50,000.
  • Entity groups (8): private_email, phone_number, person_name, address, account_number, url, date, secret.

docs.title: 1. Docker service
docs.text:
Add privacy_filter to local.yml and production.yml only — not to test.yml (image is large; tests mock the HTTP client).

# local.yml (and analogous in production.yml)
services:
  privacy_filter:
    image: ghcr.io/open-source-legal/privacy-filter:latest
    container_name: opencontracts_local_privacy_filter
    environment:
      API_KEYS: ${PRIVACY_FILTER_API_KEY:-dev-only-not-secret}
      MAX_INPUT_CHARS: "50000"
      CORS_ORIGINS: "" # not browser-facing
    restart: unless-stopped
    # NOT published to host; reachable only on the internal docker network

Add the service name to the depends_on block of django and celeryworker so it boots with the stack.

docs.title: 2. Settings + env config
docs.text:
.envs/.local/.django adds:

PRIVACY_FILTER_URL=http://privacy_filter:8000
PRIVACY_FILTER_API_KEY=dev-only-not-secret

config/settings/base.py reads them:

PRIVACY_FILTER_URL = env("PRIVACY_FILTER_URL", default="")
PRIVACY_FILTER_API_KEY = env("PRIVACY_FILTER_API_KEY", default="")
PRIVACY_FILTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = env.int("PRIVACY_FILTER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", default=30)

If PRIVACY_FILTER_URL is empty the tool returns a deterministic error string to the LLM ("Privacy-filter service is not configured for this deployment.") rather than raising.

docs.title: 3. HTTP client
docs.text:
opencontractserver/llms/tools/core_tools/_privacy_filter_client.py

class Detection(TypedDict):
    entity_group: str
    score: float
    start: int          # offset relative to the `text` arg passed to adetect_pii
    end: int
    text: str           # canonical text[start:end], not the model's `word` field

async def adetect_pii(text: str) -> list[Detection]: ...

Async-only — mirrors the existing web_search_tools.py pattern (httpx.AsyncClient). Callers in sync DB contexts should not need it; the tool's async entrypoint awaits this directly before delegating DB work to _db_sync_to_async.

Responsibilities:

  • Chunking: CHUNK_SIZE = 40_000, CHUNK_OVERLAP = 500. Iterate chunk_start = 0, 39_500, 79_000, ... until past len(text).
  • Per-chunk POST /v1/detect with X-API-Key using httpx.AsyncClient with the configured timeout.
  • Remap detection offsets within the chunk back to indices into text: start_in_text = chunk_start + det["start"].
  • Deduplicate across overlap by (start, end, entity_group).
  • Re-derive each detection's text from the input string (do not trust the model's word field — fewer surprises with whitespace and casing).
  • On non-2xx response, raise RuntimeError with status + first 200 chars of body so the agent-tool wrapper can return it as an error string.

docs.title: 4. Tool function
docs.text:
opencontractserver/llms/tools/core_tools/pii.py

ENTITY_GROUP_LABELS: dict[str, tuple[str, str, str]] = {
    "private_email":   ("PII: Email",          "#1f77b4", "mail"),
    "phone_number":    ("PII: Phone",          "#ff7f0e", "phone"),
    "person_name":     ("PII: Person Name",    "#2ca02c", "user"),
    "address":         ("PII: Address",        "#d62728", "home"),
    "account_number":  ("PII: Account Number", "#9467bd", "credit card"),
    "url":             ("PII: URL",            "#8c564b", "linkify"),
    "date":            ("PII: Date",           "#e377c2", "calendar"),
    "secret":          ("PII: Secret",         "#7f7f7f", "key"),
}

async def ascan_and_annotate_pii(
    *,
    # context-injected
    document_id: int,
    corpus_id: int,
    creator_id: int,
    corpus_action_id: int | None = None,
    # agent-controllable
    min_score: float = 0.5,
    entity_groups: list[str] | None = None,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    start_char: int | None = None,
    end_char: int | None = None,
) -> dict:
    # 1. Load doc + doc_text (sync DB) via _db_sync_to_async helper.
    # 2. await adetect_pii(slice)  — async network I/O.
    # 3. Persist annotations (sync DB) via _db_sync_to_async helper.

Splitting (1) and (3) into _db_sync_to_async-wrapped helpers keeps the async entrypoint free of SynchronousOnlyOperation risk while letting the network round-trip stay native-async, matching web_search_tools.py.

No sync public entrypoint is exposed; the tool registry only references the async name (ascan_and_annotate_pii).

Return shape:

{
  "document_id": int,
  "scanned_chars": int,
  "detection_count": int,
  "by_entity_group": {"private_email": 3, "phone_number": 1, ...},
  "annotation_ids": list[int],          # [] when dry_run
  "detections": list[dict],             # populated only when dry_run
}

Each entry in detections (dry_run only):

{"entity_group": str, "score": float, "start": int, "end": int, "text": str}

docs.title: 5. Data flow
docs.text:
ascan_and_annotate_pii(doc_id, knobs)
   │
   ├─ resolve doc + corpus, verify linkage (same as existing tool)
   ├─ load doc_text:
   │     PDF  → expand_pawls_pages + build_translation_layer; pdf_layer.doc_text
   │     text → doc.txt_extract_file.read()
   │     other → ValueError("Unsupported file_type ...")
   │
   ├─ slice = doc_text[start_char or 0 : end_char or len]
   │   (record `slice_offset = start_char or 0`)
   │
   ├─ await adetect_pii(slice) → list[Detection]  (offsets relative to slice)
   ├─ shift each offset by slice_offset → global doc_text offsets
   ├─ filter: score >= min_score AND (entity_groups is None or group in set)
   │
   ├─ if dry_run: return {detections: [...], annotation_ids: []}
   │
   └─ atomic transaction:
        for det in detections:
            label_text, color, icon = ENTITY_GROUP_LABELS[det.entity_group]
            label = corpus.ensure_label_and_labelset(
                label_text=label_text, label_type=<TOKEN_LABEL|SPAN_LABEL>,
                color=color, icon=icon, creator_id=creator_id,
            )
            PDF:  span = TextSpan(uuid4, start=g_start, end=g_end, text=doc_text[g_start:g_end])
                  oc  = pdf_layer.create_opencontract_annotation_from_span(SpanAnnotation(span, label.text))
                  Annotation(... raw_text=oc["rawText"], page=oc["page"], json=oc["annotation_json"],
                             annotation_type=TOKEN_LABEL, corpus_action_id=corpus_action_id, ...).save()
            text: Annotation(... raw_text=doc_text[g_start:g_end], page=1,
                             json={"start": g_start, "end": g_end},
                             annotation_type=SPAN_LABEL, corpus_action_id=corpus_action_id, ...).save()
            append id to annotation_ids
        return {by_entity_group, detection_count, annotation_ids, ...}

opencontractserver/llms/tools/tool_registry.py:

),

docs.title: 7. Error handling
docs.text: Failure Handling PRIVACY_FILTER_URL empty Return error string to LLM via existing fault-tolerance wrapper. HTTP transport / 5xx / /readyz failure RuntimeError → wrapper returns error string to LLM. Document not in corpus / unsupported file_type ValueError (mirrors add_annotations_from_exact_strings). Detection offset out of bounds after remap Skip, log WARNING, continue. start_char/end_char out of range Clamp to [0, len(doc_text)]; if start >= end, return zero detections. Permission failures (read-only user) Already handled upstream by the agent-tool framework.

docs.title: Testing strategy
docs.text:
All tests mock the privacy-filter HTTP client — no live container.

opencontractserver/tests/test_pii_scan_tool.py (new):

  1. PDF happy path — fixture PDF + PAWLs, mocked detections at known offsets; assert 1 annotation per detection, TOKEN_LABEL, correct annotation_label, raw_text, json["annotation_json"] non-empty.
  2. Text happy path — .txt document, assert SPAN_LABEL with json == {"start": s, "end": e}.
  3. Dry-run — dry_run=True ⇒ no Annotation rows created, detections populated, annotation_ids == [].
  4. Score threshold — min_score=0.9 filters out a 0.7 detection.
  5. Entity-group allowlist — entity_groups=["private_email"] skips phone_number detections.
  6. Char-range scope — start_char/end_char slice; offsets in returned annotations are global (not slice-relative).
  7. Chunk-boundary dedup — client receives a 41,000-char text, two chunks overlap on a person_name detection; assert exactly one annotation.
  8. Unsupported file_type — application/png raises ValueError.
  9. Service unconfigured — PRIVACY_FILTER_URL="" returns an error string, no exception bubbles to the test runner.
  10. Permission filtering — read-only user on the corpus has the tool filtered out of the resolved tool set (uses existing test helper for tool-set resolution).

Client-only unit tests in test_privacy_filter_client.py:

  • Chunking math: 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 chunks for varying input lengths.
  • Offset remap: detection at chunk-local index i of chunk N appears at global index N * (CHUNK_SIZE - CHUNK_OVERLAP) + i.
  • Dedup: identical (start, end, group) triple from two chunks → one entry.
  • 5xx response → RuntimeError.
