docs.title: In-Run History Compaction via pydantic-ai history_processors
In-Run History Compaction via pydantic-ai history_processors
docs.text: Date: 2026-05-27 Status: Approved — proceeding to implementation plan Related: PR #1814 (deep-research agent surfaced the gap)

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
PydanticAICoreAgent._get_message_history() runs the OpenContracts compaction pipeline once, at the start of agent.chat() / agent.stream(), against the persisted ChatMessage rows. The trimmed list is handed to pydantic_ai.Agent.run() (or .iter()) as message_history=….

Inside that single run() the agent loop appends a new ModelRequest and ModelResponse on every iteration. For long autonomous loops — the deep-research agent, but also any chat that does heavy tool use — that in-flight history accumulates unbounded inside pydantic-ai's loop, with no opportunity to compact. The only guard is the cumulative UsageLimits.request_tokens_limit, which terminates the run rather than reclaiming space.

The biggest contributors to in-run bloat are:

  • ToolReturnPart.content for large retrieval tools (load_document_text, similarity_search, search_exact_text_as_sources).
  • ThinkingPart.content for Claude extended thinking / OpenAI reasoning models (5–10K tokens per turn is typical).

The smallest viable fix is to wire a pydantic-ai HistoryProcessor into the single existing agent-construction chokepoint so every chat path picks it up automatically.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
In:

  • All chat paths that construct a pydantic_ai.Agent via opencontractserver.llms.agents.pydantic_ai_factory.make_pydantic_ai_agent. That's four call sites today: corpus chat (PydanticAICorpusAgent), document chat (PydanticAIDocumentAgent), structured extraction (_chat_raw's per-call sub-agent at pydantic_ai_agents.py:1714), and the deep-research agent (which goes through agents.for_corpus, so it's already in this set).
  • Streaming (_stream_core) and non-streaming (_chat_raw) entry points.

Out:

  • LlamaIndex / non-pydantic-ai agent backends (different runtime, no history_processors concept).
  • Persistent (cross-turn) compaction — that's already handled by _get_message_history() and is not changing.
  • Smarter LLM-generated summaries of dropped content — out of scope; this design only shrinks/drops in-place.
  • TextPart (model intermediate prose) — kept intact; semantically more useful than ThinkingPart, and rarely the bulk of bloat.

docs.title: New module
docs.text:
opencontractserver/llms/history_processors.py (sibling to context_guardrails.py).

Single public export:

async def shrink_old_artifacts_processor(
    ctx: RunContext[PydanticAIDependencies],
    messages: list[ModelMessage],
) -> list[ModelMessage]:
    ...

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Extend the existing CompactionConfig in context_guardrails.py with four new fields. Defaults make this on by default without changing call-site behaviour:

@dataclass
class CompactionConfig:
    # ... existing fields ...
    in_run_enabled: bool = True
    in_run_keep_recent_pairs: int = 4
    in_run_tool_return_target_chars: int = 4_000
    in_run_drop_thinking: bool = True

Validation: in_run_keep_recent_pairs >= 1, in_run_tool_return_target_chars >= 1. Reuse the existing __post_init__ style.

Backing constants (in opencontractserver/constants/context_guardrails.py) so operators can tune via settings: IN_RUN_KEEP_RECENT_PAIRS, IN_RUN_TOOL_RETURN_TARGET_CHARS, IN_RUN_DROP_THINKING_DEFAULT.

docs.title: Wiring point
docs.text:
make_pydantic_ai_agent in pydantic_ai_factory.py is the existing single chokepoint for pydantic_ai.Agent(...) construction (originally created for issue #1451). It already forbids system_prompt=; we extend it to always inject shrink_old_artifacts_processor into the history_processors= list:

def make_pydantic_ai_agent(model, *, system_prompt=_SYSTEM_PROMPT_FORBIDDEN, **kwargs):
    if system_prompt is not _SYSTEM_PROMPT_FORBIDDEN:
        raise TypeError(...)
    existing = list(kwargs.pop("history_processors", None) or [])
    kwargs["history_processors"] = [shrink_old_artifacts_processor, *existing]
    return PydanticAIAgent(model=model, **kwargs)

The processor goes first so any caller-supplied processors run on already-shrunk history (cheaper, and matches the "fast path" idiom). Existing callers pass no history_processors, so the change is additive.

docs.title: Telemetry surface
docs.text:
Add one new optional field to PydanticAIDependencies:

@dataclass
class PydanticAIDependencies:
    # ... existing fields ...
    on_in_run_shrink: Callable[[InRunShrinkEvent], None] | None = None

InRunShrinkEvent is a lightweight dataclass living next to the processor:

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InRunShrinkEvent:
    tokens_before: int
    tokens_after: int
    context_window: int
    tool_returns_shrunk: int
    thinking_parts_dropped: int

PydanticAICoreAgent._stream_core sets agent_deps.on_in_run_shrink to a closure that builds a ThoughtEvent and appends it via TimelineBuilder (mirrors the existing was_compacted notification at pydantic_ai_agents.py:960-979). _chat_raw does not set the callback → log-only telemetry. The processor unconditionally logs at INFO with the same numbers.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
The processor is invoked by pydantic-ai before every model request (see pydantic_ai/_agent_graph.py:521). On each call:

  1. Cheap pre-check — sum a token estimate over messages using estimate_token_count on the textual content of every UserPromptPart, SystemPromptPart, ToolReturnPart, TextPart, ThinkingPart, ToolCallPart it sees. Add estimate_token_count(deps.system_prompt or ""). Compare against threshold_ratio * get_context_window_for_model(deps.model_name). Under threshold → return messages unchanged. This is the hot path; existing tests must show it adds <1ms for the common case.

  2. Identify the protected suffix — the last in_run_keep_recent_pairs "pairs" of ModelResponse + ModelRequest are untouched. Pair boundaries are computed by scanning messages from the tail. The very last message must remain a ModelRequest (pydantic-ai contract at _agent_graph.py:1403).

  3. Walk the older prefix and shrink —

  4. For each ToolReturnPart whose len(content) > in_run_tool_return_target_chars: replace content with content[:target] + "\n\n…[in-run trim: {N} chars elided]". Preserve tool_call_id, tool_name, timestamp, metadata. Increment tool_returns_shrunk counter.
  5. For each ModelResponse in the older prefix, if in_run_drop_thinking: filter ThinkingPart instances out of parts. ToolCallPart and TextPart stay. Increment thinking_parts_dropped counter per part dropped.

  6. Never touch ToolCallPart — its tool_call_id must match the corresponding ToolReturnPart in the next message. Dropping the call without its return (or vice versa) triggers OpenAI 400 "tool_call_id not found".

  7. Recompute token estimate on the shrunk list. Emit telemetry: log INFO, and if deps.on_in_run_shrink is set call it with the populated InRunShrinkEvent.

  8. Return the shrunk messages list.

Mutation contract: pydantic-ai treats processor input as owned by it (see _agent_graph.py:520-525, which assigns back into ctx.state.message_history[:]). The processor SHOULD return a new list with new ModelMessage / part instances to avoid mutating caller-visible state. Use dataclasses.replace (parts are dataclasses in pydantic-ai 1.62) so the originals stay immutable.

docs.title: Edge cases
docs.text:
• History shorter than in_run_keep_recent_pairs: all messages are "recent"; no older prefix → no-op, return unchanged.
  • No ToolReturnPart or ThinkingPart in the older prefix: even if over threshold, there's nothing to shrink. Log a WARNING (this indicates a configuration mismatch — the chat is bloating from TextParts or UserPrompts we deliberately don't touch) and return unchanged.
  • deps is None: pydantic-ai allows running without deps. Skip the with-ctx variant fields (read config from module-level defaults in context_guardrails), log at DEBUG, proceed.
  • Tool-call/return pairing across messages: a ToolCallPart in ModelResponse[i] is satisfied by ToolReturnPart in ModelRequest[i+1]. Shrinking the content of the return without dropping the part itself preserves the tool_call_id correlation. This is why we shrink in place rather than drop.
  • Streaming partial state: pydantic-ai may call the processor on a partial trailing response during streaming. The "last message must be ModelRequest" invariant is enforced by pydantic-ai post-hoc (line 1403); our processor never touches the last message anyway, so we satisfy it implicitly.
  • Caller passes their own history_processors: our processor runs first, caller's run second. Caller can disable ours by passing in_run_enabled=False via CompactionConfig (the processor checks this flag and no-ops).

docs.title: Failure handling
docs.text:
• Token estimate over-counts: tolerable — over-counting causes premature shrinking (correct direction).
  • Token estimate under-counts: pydantic-ai's own UsageLimits.request_tokens_limit is the backstop; if our threshold-based shrink fails to kick in early enough, the run still terminates cleanly.
  • Processor itself raises: pydantic-ai surfaces this as a user-facing exception (no catch in _process_message_history). The OpenContracts CoreAgentBase.chat() wrapper catches all exceptions and returns an Error: … UnifiedChatResponse — so a processor bug is a degraded chat experience, not a hard crash. The processor is written to be defensive (try/except around the per-message walk, with a logger.exception + return-original fallback).

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
All new tests live under opencontractserver/tests/llms/test_history_processors.py. Use plain pytest (not Django TestCase) — the processor is a pure function over pydantic-ai messages.

Unit-level (no DB, no LLM):

  1. test_under_threshold_returns_unchanged — synthesise a list of 10 messages with small tool returns; assert the processor returns the same list (identity or deep-equal) and emits no telemetry.
  2. test_shrinks_old_tool_returns_when_over_threshold — synthesise 20 messages, large ToolReturnPart.content in the first 10; assert older returns are truncated to target_chars + notice, recent N are untouched, tool_returns_shrunk count matches.
  3. test_drops_older_thinking_parts — synthesise messages with ThinkingPart throughout; assert older ThinkingParts are gone, recent ones are kept, ToolCallPart/TextPart siblings survive.
  4. test_preserves_tool_call_id_correlation — synthesise a ToolCallPart/ToolReturnPart pair; assert post-shrink the tool_call_id is unchanged and the return part still exists (just shrunk).
  5. test_last_message_is_modelrequest_invariant — verify the processor never touches the last message.
  6. test_history_shorter_than_keep_recent_pairs — 3 messages with keep_recent_pairs=4; no-op even if individually over threshold.
  7. test_no_shrinkable_content_logs_and_returns_unchanged — over threshold but no ToolReturnPart and no ThinkingPart; assert WARNING logged, list returned unchanged.
  8. test_in_run_enabled_false_short_circuits — CompactionConfig(in_run_enabled=False); assert no-op even when far over threshold.
  9. test_telemetry_callback_called_with_correct_counts — assert on_in_run_shrink is invoked exactly once per shrink with populated InRunShrinkEvent.

Integration (existing pattern, with mocked LLM):

  1. test_make_pydantic_ai_agent_injects_processor — call make_pydantic_ai_agent(...) with no history_processors; assert the constructed Agent has shrink_old_artifacts_processor in agent.history_processors.
  2. test_caller_processors_run_after_ours — pass history_processors=[caller_proc]; assert order in resulting agent is [shrink_old_artifacts_processor, caller_proc].
  3. test_stream_emits_thoughtevent_on_shrink — extend tests/test_pydantic_ai_factory.py (or a new test_in_run_shrink_telemetry.py) to run a streamed chat with a forced large tool return, assert a ThoughtEvent with metadata["in_run_shrink"] appears in the timeline.

Regression:

  1. test_existing_compaction_test_suite_passes_unchanged — run the full opencontractserver/tests/llms/ suite to confirm the pre-run _get_message_history compaction path is unaffected.
  2. test_pydantic_ai_factory_existing_assertions — test_pydantic_ai_factory.py still passes (the system_prompt guard, model kwarg passthrough, etc.).

Manual smoke:

  1. Deep-research run against a non-trivial corpus with a deliberately verbose retrieval task; observe the log for in-run shrink events and confirm the report still finalises with citations intact.

docs.title: Migration & rollout
docs.text:
• New code only; no DB migration.
  • Defaults make the processor active immediately for every chat. The in_run_enabled knob is the kill switch if a regression appears.
  • No backwards-compat shim needed — the factory already centralises agent construction.
  • CHANGELOG entry under ## [Unreleased] describing the new in-run compaction behaviour and the new CompactionConfig fields.

docs.title: Files touched
docs.text:
• opencontractserver/llms/history_processors.py — new, the processor + InRunShrinkEvent.
  • opencontractserver/llms/context_guardrails.py — extend CompactionConfig with four new fields + validation.
  • opencontractserver/constants/context_guardrails.py — add IN_RUN_* constants.
  • opencontractserver/llms/agents/pydantic_ai_factory.py — inject the processor in make_pydantic_ai_agent.
  • opencontractserver/llms/agents/pydantic_ai_agents.py — add on_in_run_shrink field to PydanticAIDependencies; wire the closure in _stream_core so the stream timeline shows the event.
  • opencontractserver/tests/llms/test_history_processors.py — new, unit tests.
  • opencontractserver/tests/test_pydantic_ai_factory.py — extend with the two new assertions.
  • CHANGELOG.md — entry under ## [Unreleased].

docs.title: Acceptance criteria
docs.text:
1. make_pydantic_ai_agent returns an Agent whose history_processors starts with shrink_old_artifacts_processor.
  2. A simulated 200K-token history with 10 oversized ToolReturnParts in the older prefix is shrunk to under 80% of the model's context window in a single processor call.
  3. tool_call_id correlation between every ToolCallPart and its corresponding ToolReturnPart is unchanged after shrinking.
  4. Streamed chats emit a ThoughtEvent carrying InRunShrinkEvent data when a shrink fires; non-streamed chats produce only an INFO log line.
  5. The pre-run compaction path (_get_message_history) is bit-identical: same callers, same outputs, same persisted bookmarks.
  6. in_run_enabled=False reverts behaviour to pre-design (processor no-ops on every call).

docs.title: Scope Admin (Superuser) Data Access — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-05-31 Branch: security/scope-admin-data-access Status: Approved for implementation

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
A is_superuser account today receives a blanket bypass throughout the data-permission layer: it can READ every row of every data model and pass every user_can check on every object, regardless of ownership, sharing, is_public, or corpus membership. This is implemented as ~15 if user.is_superuser: return self.all() / return True short-circuits scattered across managers, querysets, query optimizers, the permission-utility layer, and the GraphQL permission mixin.

The goal: an admin's access to user data (corpuses, documents, annotations, relationships, notes, conversations, analyses, extracts, folders, datacells, feedback, user profiles, badge awards) must be computed identically to any other user. Admins retain elevated rights only over genuinely admin-only system/config objects.

docs.title: Resolved Design Decisions
docs.text:
1. Structural items — narrow break-glass exception (KEEP). Structural annotations/relationships remain system-managed and immutable for ordinary users. The one retained superuser data-write privilege is the ability to write (CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE) structural annotations & relationships, so an admin can repair bad structural data through the app. This is enforced in AnnotationManager.user_can / RelationshipManager.user_can as a narrow exception inside the existing structural-write-deny branch — it is not a general data bypass. Everything else (READ visibility, non-structural writes) is computed for a superuser exactly as for a normal user.

  2. User profiles — treat as normal data. Remove the UserProfileManager superuser bypass; admins see private profiles only via the same corpus-membership rule as anyone else. Badge-awarding (the documented consumer of that bypass) is reworked to resolve the recipient through an explicit authorize-then-unfiltered-lookup path so it no longer depends on admin profile visibility.

  3. Break-glass = Django admin site. The Django admin site (is_staff) uses unfiltered ORM and is unaffected by these manager changes; it remains the proper, audited path for an admin who genuinely must inspect/repair arbitrary user data. A follow-up to add an explicit, audited support/impersonation mechanism is flagged but out of scope here.

  4. Admin identity = is_superuser only. No is_staff/is_superuser split is introduced. The admin-only config gates keep using is_superuser.

docs.title: What stays admin-only (UNCHANGED)
docs.text:
These are gated in their GraphQL mutation resolvers, not in the data managers, so they are untouched by this change:

  • PipelineSettings (parser/embedder/thumbnailer/enricher config + encrypted secrets) — config/graphql/pipeline_settings_mutations.py
  • Badge definitions + award/revoke management — config/graphql/badge_mutations.py
  • CorpusCategory taxonomy management — config/graphql/corpus_category_mutations.py

CorpusCategory rows remain globally readable (no change); only their mutation remains superuser-gated.

docs.title: The New Rule (one sentence)
docs.text: A superuser is authorized over data exactly as a normal user, with a single retained exception — it may write structural annotations and relationships — and it keeps superuser-gated control of admin-only config objects via their existing mutation-level checks.

docs.title: A. Visibility managers / querysets — remove superuser bypass
docs.text:
Remove the if user.is_superuser: return self.all() (and the prefetch/distinct opt-outs that exist because superusers used to skip the permission JOINs). After removal, superusers flow through the same guardian JOIN / is_public / creator / membership logic as everyone else, so they also need the prefetch + distinct that were previously skipped.

Site File Action BaseVisibilityManager.visible_to_user shared/Managers.py remove superuser early-return; remove and not user.is_superuser guards on prefetch + distinct PermissionQuerySet.visible_to_user shared/QuerySets.py remove superuser early-return DocumentQuerySet.visible_to_user shared/QuerySets.py remove AnnotationQuerySet.visible_to_user shared/QuerySets.py remove (admins lose trashed-doc visibility via app; use Django admin) NoteQuerySet.visible_to_user shared/QuerySets.py remove UserFeedbackQuerySet.visible_to_user shared/QuerySets.py remove PermissionedTreeQuerySet.visible_to_user shared/QuerySets.py remove RelationshipManager.visible_to_user shared/Managers.py remove superuser branch so superusers flow through the normal MIN(doc,corpus) logic UserProfileManager.visible_to_user users/models.py remove superuser branch

docs.title: B. Single-object user_can — remove blanket bypass; keep structural exception
C. Permission enumeration + GraphQL mixin
docs.text: Site File Action get_users_permissions_for_obj (creator branch + guardian branch) utils/permissioning.py remove both superuser branches; superusers get the same computed permission set as any user AnnotatePermissionsForReadMixin.resolve_my_permissions config/graphql/permissioning/permission_annotator/mixins.py remove the superuser branch that injects synthetic "superuser" + folds in all model perms

docs.title: D. Query optimizers — remove superuser short-circuits
docs.text:
Site File Action AnnotationQueryOptimizer._compute_effective_permissions annotations/query_optimizer.py remove if is_superuser: return True,True,True,True; compute normally MetadataQueryOptimizer superuser branches extracts/query_optimizer.py remove DocumentActionsQueryOptimizer._check_document_permission / _check_corpus_permission documents/query_optimizer.py remove "user is superuser" grant Any superuser branch in extract/analysis/relationship optimizer methods surfaced by the test sweep respective optimizer files remove

my_permissions for structural items therefore reads read-only for everyone (including admins) in the optimizer-driven display path; the structural-write break-glass lives only at the user_can/mutation layer. This is acceptable and documented (the frontend already renders structural items read-only).

docs.title: E. Badge awarding rework (decouple from profile visibility)
docs.text:
config/graphql/badge_mutations.py AwardBadgeMutation currently does:

recipient = get_for_user_or_none(User, recipient_pk, awarder)  # privacy-filtered

Rework to authorize the awarder first, then resolve the recipient unfiltered:

# 1. existing awarder authorization (superuser for global badges,
#    corpus owner/editor for corpus badges) runs first.
# 2. recipient lookup is a direct system lookup — awarding to a
#    private-profile recipient is legitimate once awarding is authorized.
recipient = User.objects.filter(pk=recipient_pk, is_active=True).first()
if recipient is None:
    return AwardBadgeMutation(ok=False, message="User not found", user_badge=None)

BadgeService.get_visible_user_badges superuser short-circuit is removed — badge awards (UserBadge) are user data and follow normal profile-privacy visibility for admins too.

docs.title: F. users/models.py "inactive users visible to superuser" note
docs.text: The profile manager filters is_active=True. After removing the superuser branch, inactive users are not visible to anyone via the app (consistent — use Django admin). Update the doc accordingly.

docs.title: Documentation Changes (consolidated_permissioning_guide.md)
docs.text:
Rewrite every "except for superusers" / "superusers bypass all permission checks" passage to the new rule. Concretely:

  • Replace the global structural banner (line 5) and the "Superuser Access — bypass all permission checks" section (≈ 976-980) with the one-sentence new rule + the narrow structural exception.
  • Fix the Can Access / can_read = is_superuser OR ... formula blocks (≈ 411, 438, 529, 556, 580, 672) — superuser is no longer a disjunct for data reads; it is replaced by an explicit note that superusers are computed as normal users for data.
  • Structural-items table (≈ 643-648): keep "Superuser = Full CRUD" for structural rows only; clarify non-structural rows now read "same as a normal user" for superusers.
  • _compute_effective_permissions example (≈ 900-901): drop the if user.is_superuser: return True,True,True,True block.
  • UserProfileManager "Do not remove it" note (≈ 1163): replace with "profiles are normal data; admins see private profiles only via shared-corpus membership; badge awarding resolves recipients via an authorize-then-lookup path."
  • Metadata "Superusers: Full access" (≈ 518), document-actions "Superuser access to all documents" (≈ 1391), get_for_user_or_none (≈ 2169) superuser line: update to the new rule.
  • Add a new "Admin (Superuser) Access Model" section near the top stating the rule, the structural exception, the admin-only config list, and the Django-admin break-glass path + flagged follow-up.
  • The "adding a new model" recipe (≈ 2757-2758) and invariant-mixin docs: update the superuser fixture guidance to reflect that the mixin's superuser test now asserts normal-user semantics for data + the structural exception, not blanket access.

docs.title: Test Changes (blast radius ≈ 40-50 methods, 25+ files)
docs.text:
The authorization-invariant suite and per-area permission tests currently pin "superuser sees/does everything." Each must be updated to the new contract. Two patterns:

  1. Tests that assert blanket superuser visibility/authority over data — rewrite to assert a superuser with no grants is treated like a stranger (sees only public/own/shared), and add a positive case where a superuser with normal grants behaves like a granted user.
  2. Structural read-only tests — keep asserting the superuser CAN write structural items (the retained exception); add assertions that a superuser cannot READ a structural item on a document it has no access to (data parity).

Key files (non-exhaustive; full list enumerated during implementation):

  • tests/permissioning/test_authorization_invariants.py — _UserCanInvariantsMixin.test_superuser_bypass_all_permissions becomes a data-parity test; structural subclasses keep the structural-write assertion; CorpusAuthorizationInvariantsTestCase superuser tests rewritten.
  • tests/permissioning/test_base_model_permissions.py, test_permissioned_querysets.py, test_get_for_user_or_none.py, test_creator_based_permissions.py, test_comment_permission.py, test_corpus_visibility.py, test_feedback_mutations.py, test_user_visibility.py, test_badge_visibility.py, test_badges.py, test_document_actions_permissions.py, test_metadata_query_optimizer.py, test_permission_optimizer.py, test_query_optimizer_methods.py, test_analysis_extract_hybrid_permissions.py, test_annotation_permission_inheritance.py, test_annotation_privacy_scoping.py, test_authorization_invariants_coverage.py, test_permissioning.py.
  • test_badges.py::test_non_superuser_cannot_award_to_private_profile_recipient changes meaning: after the rework, the relevant assertion becomes "an authorized awarder (superuser or corpus owner) can award to a private recipient via the unfiltered lookup; an unauthorized caller is rejected at the awarder-authorization gate (not via profile visibility)."

New regression tests to add:

  • superuser_with_no_grants_sees_only_public_and_own (Corpus, Document, Annotation, Note, Relationship, Conversation, Feedback) — the core anti-leak guarantee.
  • superuser_cannot_read_private_stranger_data for profiles + badge awards.
  • superuser_may_write_structural_but_not_read_inaccessible_structural.

docs.title: Approach / Sequencing
docs.text:
1. Land the invariant + new regression tests expressing the new contract (they fail against current code).
  2. Apply production changes A–F until the invariant suite is green.
  3. Sweep the wider permission test files, updating each superuser assertion to the new contract (parallelizable per-file).
  4. Rewrite the guide.
  5. Run the permissioning test subset (tests/permissioning/ + the named query- optimizer/badge tests) — not the full 30-min suite — plus pre-commit.
  6. Changelog entry.

docs.title: Out of Scope / Follow-ups
docs.text:
• Explicit audited support/impersonation mechanism (flagged, decision #3).
  • Any is_staff vs is_superuser split (decision #4 keeps is_superuser).
  • Celery/system-context callers that pass no user or a system user are unaffected (they never relied on is_superuser).

docs.title: PDF Chunking Pipeline Redesign — Design Spec
PDF Chunking Pipeline Redesign — Design Spec
docs.text: Date: 2026-06-07 Status: Approved (design); pending implementation plan Branch: feature/pdf-chunking-pipeline

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
Large PDFs strain the parser pipeline on three axes at once:

  1. Memory — the whole PDF, all chunk results, and the full reassembled document can be resident in RAM simultaneously, risking OOM on big docs.
  2. Throughput — chunk parsing is in-process (max_concurrent_chunks, default 3) on a single worker, so large docs do not benefit from the worker fleet.
  3. Generalization — page-range chunking exists only in the Docling REST parser (DoclingParser(BaseChunkedParser)); no other parser can reuse it.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: Make N-page batch parsing a shared, opt-in capability for PDF-producing parsers that (a) bounds memory, (b) parallelises across Celery workers, and © preserves structure that spans chunk boundaries via overlap windows.

docs.title: Scope decisions (from brainstorming)
docs.text:
• Primary driver: all three goals (memory + throughput + generalization).
  • Boundary handling: overlap windows — each chunk overlaps its neighbour by overlap pages so boundary-spanning structure is captured whole in at least one chunk; dedupe on reassembly.
  • Parser scope: PDF parsers, opt-in. Build chunking as a shared mixin/base any parser can opt into. Docling (already chunked) plus any other in-process PDF parser opt in. DOCX (docxodus) and TXT (oc_text_parser) explicitly opt out — they are not paginated. Remote APIs that self-batch (LlamaParse) are left as-is.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
• Re-architecting DOCX/TXT character-offset parsing.
  • Forcing LlamaParse through our splitter (it does its own batching).
  • True O(1) memory for the final saved document (see "Honest memory bound").

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
ChunkingStrategy (format-aware split, with overlap)
        │
        ▼
Celery chord:  group(parse_chunk_task × N)  ──►  reassemble_chunks_task (callback)
        │                                                │
   each chunk: parse → write result to storage,    stream chunk results back
   return only the storage key                     one at a time → dedupe →
                                                    re-link → save_parsed_data()

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
1. ChunkingStrategy — extend opencontractserver/utils/pdf_splitting.py with calculate_page_chunks_with_overlap(total_pages, max_pages_per_chunk, min_pages_for_chunking, overlap) returning ranges annotated with their overlap lead/tail so the reassembler knows which pages are duplicates. For non-paginated formats the strategy returns a single whole-document chunk, so the orchestration path is uniform and opt-out parsers flow through unchanged.

  2. ChunkedParserMixin — generalised from today's BaseChunkedParser. A parser opts in with supports_chunking = True and implements _parse_single_chunk_impl(chunk_bytes, page_offset, **kwargs). Docling already implements this contract.

  3. parse_chunk_task (new Celery task) — parses one chunk and writes its OpenContractDocExport to default storage under tmp/chunks/{doc_id}/{chunk_idx}.json, returning only the storage key (a small string). Idempotent on the key so retries are safe.

  4. reassemble_chunks_task (chord callback) — streams chunk results in page order, one at a time: offsets global page indices, dedupes overlap pages (by global index) and annotations (by (label, page, bbox/span signature)), re-links boundary-spanning relationships via global annotation IDs, then hands the combined OpenContractDocExport to the existing save_parsed_data(). Cleans up tmp/chunks/{doc_id}/ in a finally.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text: ingest_doc resolves the parser. If the parser does not support chunking, or page_count < min_pages_for_chunking, the current single-shot path runs unchanged. Otherwise: build overlapping ranges → dispatch a Celery chord (group of parse_chunk_task, callback reassemble_chunks_task).

docs.title: Honest memory bound
docs.text:
This redesign does not achieve literal O(1) memory, and the spec is explicit about that:

  • Per worker: peak = one chunk's PDF bytes + one chunk's parsed result.
  • Reassembler: peak = one chunk result at a time + the growing combined document (which must exist to be saved by save_parsed_data() / compact_pawls_pages() / import_annotations()).

So the realistic bound is "one chunk at a time + one final document," not "all chunk PDFs + all raw results + final document simultaneously" as today. That is the phase-1 win.

A phase-4 (optional) aggressive variant imports each chunk's annotations into the DB as the chunk lands, making the DB the accumulator so reassembler RAM stays bounded by a single chunk. Deferred because it complicates dedup (cross-chunk dedup at the DB level) and index reconciliation; not required for the headline win.

docs.title: Overlap & dedup
docs.text:
• overlap default: 2 pages. Constraint: overlap must exceed the largest expected boundary-spanning structure, or a relationship can still be severed. Residual orphaned relationships/parent_ids after dedup are logged + metricked, never fatal.
  • Chunking stays gated at the current 75-page threshold (min_pages_for_chunking), max_pages_per_chunk default unchanged (50).
  • Page dedup: keep first occurrence by global page index.
  • Annotation dedup: within overlap zones, collapse on (label, page, bbox/span signature).
  • Relationship re-linking: resolve endpoints against the deduped global annotation ID set after pages/annotations are merged.

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• A parse_chunk_task failure retries that chunk (Celery retry, idempotent storage key) — not the whole document. The chord fails only if a chunk exhausts its retries.
  • Existing Docling permanent-vs-transient 5xx classification (_DOCLING_PERMANENT_FAILURE_SIGNATURES) is preserved per chunk so a malformed PDF fails fast instead of triggering a retry storm.
  • Temp chunk artifacts are always cleaned up in the reassembler's finally, including on failure paths.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Golden equivalence test (correctness gate): parse a real multi-page PDF chunked-with-overlap vs single-shot and assert identical PAWLs pages, annotations, and relationships. This is the gate that proves chunking is lossless.
  • Unit tests: overlap range math, page dedup, annotation dedup, global page-index offsetting, cross-boundary relationship re-linking.
  • A memory/parallelism test asserting the reassembler holds at most one chunk result in memory at a time (bounded peak), and that chunks dispatch as independent tasks.

docs.title: Rollout (phased — feature branch + per-phase tracking issues)
docs.text:
1. Phase 1 — generalise the splitter (calculate_page_chunks_with_overlap)
  2. ChunkedParserMixin + the golden equivalence test. Behaviour-preserving for Docling.
  3. Phase 2 — Celery chord fan-out + storage-backed per-chunk results + streaming reassembly (parse_chunk_task, reassemble_chunks_task).
  4. Phase 3 — overlap windows + dedup + boundary relationship re-linking.
  5. Phase 4 (optional) — DB-streaming memory variant for true one-chunk-bounded reassembler RAM.

Each phase is its own PR against feature/pdf-chunking-pipeline with a tracking issue.

docs.title: CAML-composed Corpus Intelligence — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-06-09 Branch: feature/caml-composed-intelligence (stacks on PR #1969 claude/doc-intelligence-ux-audit-mmqe14) Status: Approved (brainstorming) → implementing

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: The Corpus Intelligence overview (insight panel + document graph + ask-across-docs) and the Readme.CAML article are mutually exclusive on the corpus home: CorpusHome.tsx renders CorpusArticleView when a Readme.CAML exists, otherwise CorpusLandingView (which carries the overview). Every corpus produced by the edgar-fetch pipeline ships a Readme.CAML, so those corpora never show the overview at all.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text:
Make the intelligence overview first-class inside CAML so it composes with authored narrative — present by default, composable by authors, never silently absent — without losing CAML rendering.

Decisions (brainstorming): Hybrid composition (deterministic structural default + narrative override via the existing editor); granular embed primitives; phased delivery on a new branch.

docs.title: 1. Embed primitives (frontend)
docs.text:
Register three components in CAML_COMPONENTS (frontend/src/utils/camlComponentRegistry.ts):

Marker Renders [component:insight-panel] IntelligencePanel [component:document-graph] DocumentGraphGlimpse (self-fetching wrapper) [component:ask-across-docs] suggestion chips → corpus chat

Components are corpus-scoped. Rather than make authors type a global id, a new CamlEmbedContext (frontend/src/components/corpuses/caml/CamlEmbedContext.tsx) provides { corpusId, onAskQuestion?, onExploreGraph? }. CorpusArticleView and the CamlArticleEditor preview wrap their CAML render tree in this provider. Embeds read context; a marker corpusId= prop remains an override.

ask-across-docs routes through onAskQuestion, bound to the article's existing floating chat — no duplicate chat affordance.

docs.title: 2. Deterministic structural block (backend + shared constant)
docs.text: A code-owned CAML fragment — an "At a glance" heading plus the three oc-component fences — is the source of truth for the default. Lives in backend constants. build_default_readme_caml(corpus) returns # {title} {description} {INTELLIGENCE_BLOCK}. New corpora get a structural Readme.CAML immediately (no LLM). The LLM branding agent (generate_corpus_branding) is the rich narrative path; its output is post-processed to ensure the block is present (append if the agent omitted it). Embeds fetch live data, so the block never goes stale.

docs.title: 3. Override
docs.text: Editing Readme.CAML in CamlArticleEditor (already built) is the override. Authors reorder/drop/interleave the primitives with prose. Deleting the block is a deliberate opt-out.

docs.title: 4. Backfill + reconcile
docs.text: A management command injects the block into existing corpora's Readme.CAML (or generates a structural one where absent); idempotent. CorpusLandingView's overview injection becomes the no-CAML fallback only (kept, not deleted — it still serves corpora where generation hasn't run / failed).

docs.title: 5. Testing
docs.text:
• Frontend: CT that a CAML source with the markers renders the embeds via the registry; ask-across-docs calls the context handler. Reuses the component-level tests from PR #1969.
  • Backend: default README contains the block; branding post-processing re-inserts an omitted block; backfill is idempotent and doesn't clobber author edits.

docs.title: Phasing
docs.text:
• P1 — embeds + CamlEmbedContext + wiring + CT. An authored CAML can now show the overview. Independently shippable.
  • P2 — deterministic structural default + branding preserves the block.
  • P3 — backfill existing corpora + reconcile CorpusLandingView to fallback.

docs.title: Out of scope / YAGNI
docs.text:
• No composite corpus-intelligence block (granular only).
  • No migration off the interim marker system to upstream customBlocks (#1172).
  • No regeneration-on-data-change (embeds are live).

docs.title: Corpus Reference Enrichment Agent — Design
docs.text: Date: 2026-06-09 Branch: feature/corpus-reference-enrichment (local, off origin/main) Status: Approved design; pre-implementation-plan

docs.title: 1. Problem & Goal
docs.text:
OpenContracts corpora (e.g. an SEC Form S-1 filing with its exhibits) are full of explicit references that today are invisible to the system as connections:

  • A primary S-1 cites its own exhibits ("Exhibit 10.1", the Certificate of Incorporation, the 2021 Credit Agreement).
  • Sections cite other sections ("See \"Risk Factors\"", "as described under Use of Proceeds").
  • Documents cite external law ("Section 145 of the Delaware General Corporation Law", "Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act").
  • Defined terms ("the Company", "Sponsor") are used across sections/documents.

Goal: an agentic enrichment workflow, triggerable as a tool in chat (like the CAML writer), that crawls a corpus, inventories these references, annotates them, and creates the connecting relationships — reusing existing OpenContracts infrastructure wherever possible. References to external law must be normalized into a stub that can be tracked and joined cross-corpus later (cross-corpus linking is not supported today, but the data shape must anticipate it). The agent is v1; the same engine must be reusable in other ways later (e.g. a batch CorpusAction).

This must be proven on a real S-1 corpus — specifically the loaded corpus id=19 ("Fervo Energy … Form S-1", which actually bundles Cerebras + Fervo S-1 primary documents and ~130 exhibits).

docs.title: 2. Grounding facts (verified against the codebase and corpus 19)
docs.text: These findings shaped every decision below. They are load-bearing.

docs.title: 2.1 Data-model constraints (verified in opencontractserver/annotations/models.py)
docs.text:
• A Relationship cannot span two documents. A DB CheckConstraint (relationship_has_single_parent) and clean() force exactly one parent: either a document OR a structural_set, never both/neither. Permissioning (RelationshipManager.user_can) assumes its annotations resolve to that one document. → Within-document section→section links map onto Relationship; cross-document and cross-corpus links do not.
  • Annotation.link_url is a validated field (validate_link_url): only http(s):// absolute URLs and site-relative paths beginning with / are allowed (javascript:/data: rejected). The frontend (frontend/src/components/annotator/utils/urlAnnotation.ts) renders these clickable; site-relative paths route in-app via the SPA router (navigate()), external URLs open in a new tab with noopener,noreferrer. → A site-relative link_url like /corpus/19/document/146 is a ready-made, safe, in-app cross-document link mechanism.
  • Annotation.data is a JSONField "structured metadata sidecar" (first consumer: geocoding stamps {canonical_name, lat, lng, …} on OC_COUNTRY/OC_STATE/OC_CITY). Untyped, application-owned shape. → The sanctioned home for a normalized law payload {authority, section, canonical_key}.
  • Analysis can be created programmatically with an in-process (task_name-based, not remote-gremlin) Analyzer. Both Annotation and Relationship carry analysis (provenance/visibility) and created_by_analysis (privacy). → Provenance container for an enrichment run, enabling grouping, re-run, and cleanup.
  • Programmatic creation pattern (from opencontractserver/llms/tools/core_tools/annotations.py and document_indexing.py): corpus.ensure_label_and_labelset(...) → build unsaved Annotation(...) → set data/long_description → .save(); hierarchy via a second pass setting parent_id. Span format {"start": int, "end": int} for text docs; token JSON for PDFs.

docs.title: 2.2 Corpus-19 reality (verified by querying the dev DB and reading text)
docs.text:
• 130 documents: a ~900 KB primary S-1 plus exhibits (Ex 3.1 Certificate of Incorporation, 3.2 bylaws, 10.x material contracts, 21.1, 23.1, …).
  • Reference patterns confirmed present in the real text:
  • Law: 9× "… Delaware General Corporation Law" (incl. "Section 145 of …", "Section 203 of …"); "Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act", "Section 7(a)(2)(B) …", "Section 8(a) …".
  • Internal section refs: 49× See "…" / See the section … (incl. See "Risk Factors").
  • Doc↔Doc: exhibit references + an exhibit index.
  • Existing structure to reuse, not reinvent: label breakdown shows EXHIBIT_REFERENCE (15), Exhibit doc-type (126), SEC_HEADER (130), S-1 (130), OC_SECTION (20).
  • EXHIBIT_REFERENCE spans already mark "Exhibit 1.1" etc. but carry no link_url and no data — detection is partly done, resolution/linking is the gap this agent fills.
  • Zero annotations corpus-wide have link_url set — cross-doc linking is greenfield here.
  • OC_SECTION is sparse: 5/130 docs, 20 annotations, mostly-null parent. → The resolver must NOT assume a dense section index; it needs a heading-text fallback (and may optionally invoke the existing create_document_index tool to build an index when absent).

docs.title: 2.3 Reusable agent infrastructure (verified)
docs.text:
• CoreTool → PydanticAIToolWrapper with requires_corpus, requires_write_permission, requires_approval, parameter injection (document_id/corpus_id/user_id hidden from the LLM), per-call permission checks, and tool-output truncation. Register in tool_registry.py (AVAILABLE_TOOLS + FUNCTION_MAP).
  • PydanticAICorpusAgent (corpus-scoped) attaches corpus tools; the WebSocket consumer (config/websocket/consumers/unified_agent_conversation.py) already streams any tool's calls/approvals — no consumer changes needed.
  • The CAML writer (core_tools/caml_article.py) is the blueprint: read → propose → apply (requires_approval=True), writing back via ORM inside transaction.atomic().

docs.title: 3. Architecture
docs.text:
Deterministic engine, agent as orchestrator (chosen "Approach A" over LLM-driven crawl and pure-embedding-graph alternatives — see §9).

Agent chat (corpus-scoped PydanticAICorpusAgent)
  │  scan_corpus_references(...)                    read-only  → inventory, no writes
  │  apply_corpus_reference_enrichment(...)         approval-gated write
  ▼
Services  (new package: opencontractserver/enrichment/)   pure, testable, service-layer compliant
  ReferenceExtractor   document text → typed candidate spans (grammars/regex)
  ReferenceResolver    candidate → concrete target (OC_SECTION index, doc titles, similarity_search)
  EnrichmentWriter     persist all rows in ONE transaction under an Analysis
  ▼
Persistence  (reuse existing + ONE new model)
  Annotation        mention span; label by type; normalized `data`; link_url when internal target
  Relationship      WITHIN-document section→section & definition→usage (renders today)
  CorpusReference   NEW first-class stub: cross-doc / cross-corpus / external-law
  Analysis          provenance container for the whole run (re-run / cleanup / visibility)

Division of labor (DRY, no overlap): - Within-document links → existing Relationship (already rendered in the viewer). - Cross-boundary + external-law links → new CorpusReference. - Every reference (all types) → a mention Annotation so there is always a visible, clickable anchor in the document.

docs.title: 4. New model: CorpusReference
docs.text:
Lives in the annotations app (alongside Annotation/Relationship) to avoid new-app registration churn. Extends BaseOCModel (standard guardian permissioning, creator, is_public, timestamps).

Field Type Purpose corpus FK Corpus source corpus reference_type char choices: LAW / DOCUMENT / SECTION / DEFINED_TERM discriminator source_annotation FK Annotation (CASCADE) the mention span (always set) target_annotation FK Annotation, null=True resolved internal target target_document FK Document, null=True resolved target document target_corpus FK Corpus, null=True future cross-corpus target canonical_key CharField(255), db_index, null=True cross-corpus join key: dgcl:145, securities-act:4(a)(2), term:change-of-control normalized_data JSONField, null=True {authority, section, …} / candidate list when unresolved confidence FloatField, default 1.0 resolver confidence resolution_status char choices: RESOLVED / UNRESOLVED / EXTERNAL EXTERNAL for law; UNRESOLVED when ambiguous created_by_analysis FK Analysis, null=True provenance/run grouping

Constraints/indexes: - index on (corpus, reference_type) and on canonical_key (cross-corpus joins). - A natural-key uniqueness guard for idempotency — see §7.

GraphQL: a read-only CorpusReferenceType + a corpus-scoped resolver (through a CorpusReferenceService). No mutations in v1 (creation is via the enrichment tool). A full frontend panel is out of scope for v1 (§8).

docs.title: 5. Reference types → detect / normalize / store
docs.text:
Type Detect (extractor) Normalize Store Law grammar: Section <N> of the <DGCL\|Delaware General Corporation Law\|Securities Act\|Securities Exchange Act\|Internal Revenue Code> (+ common variants) canonical_key (dgcl:145, securities-act:4(a)(2), exchange-act:…, irc:409a); normalized_data={authority,section} mention Annotation (label OC_REF_LAW, data=normalized) + CorpusReference(LAW, EXTERNAL) Doc↔Doc reuse/extend existing EXHIBIT_REFERENCE spans + exhibit cues ("Exhibit 10.1", "our Certificate of Incorporation") match exhibit number / title → target document in corpus set mention link_url=/corpus/<cid>/document/<did> + CorpusReference(DOCUMENT, RESOLVED) Internal section See "<Heading>", See the section …, under "<Heading>" resolve heading → OC_SECTION annotation (or heading-text fallback in same doc) within-doc Relationship + mention link_url to the section anchor Defined term (opt-in, capped) definition: "<Term>" means … / shall mean; usages: subsequent capitalized occurrences term:<slug> within-doc definition→usage Relationship; cross-doc usage → CorpusReference(DEFINED_TERM)

Notes: - Mentions are non-structural (structural=False) so they're editable/ deletable by users with corpus write. - Where an EXHIBIT_REFERENCE span already exists for a detected doc reference, extend it (set link_url, create the CorpusReference) rather than creating a duplicate mention. - Section resolution degrades gracefully when OC_SECTION is absent: fall back to locating the heading text within the document and anchoring the link to that offset; optionally trigger create_document_index first.

docs.title: 6. Agent surface (CAML-style read → approval-gated apply)
docs.text:
Two new CoreTools, registered in tool_registry.py, attached to the corpus-scoped agent:

  • scan_corpus_references(corpus_id, types=[...], sample_n=...)
  • requires_corpus=True, read-only.

  • Runs ReferenceExtractor + ReferenceResolver across the corpus; returns an inventory: counts by type, sample resolved candidates, and the unresolved/ambiguous ones. No writes. Lets the user/LLM review before committing (mirrors read_corpus_caml_article / propose_caml_citation_match).

  • apply_corpus_reference_enrichment(corpus_id, types=[...])

  • requires_corpus=True, requires_write_permission=True, requires_approval=True.
  • Creates the Analysis (in-process analyzer), then all mention annotations, Relationships, and CorpusReferences in one transaction. Returns created counts + ids (mirrors apply_caml_article_edit).

The WebSocket consumer already streams tool calls and the single approval gate — no consumer changes. The same EnrichmentWriter is later wrappable as a CorpusAction for batch/scheduled runs (the "eventually other ways" path) with no redesign.

docs.title: 7. Data flow, error handling, idempotency
docs.text:
• Flow: chat → scan (inventory, no writes) → user approves → apply (transactional writes under an Analysis) → results visible (OC_URL links clickable; Relationships render; CorpusReferences queryable via GraphQL).
  • Fault tolerance (issue #820): operational errors are caught and returned as strings to the LLM; security errors (PermissionError, ToolConfirmationRequired) propagate. Per-document failures are isolated (skip + log) and never abort the whole run.
  • Idempotent re-run: dedupe by natural key (document_id, span_hash, label, canonical_key); re-running enriches only new references and creates zero duplicates. A DB unique guard on the equivalent CorpusReference tuple backs this.
  • Ambiguous targets: when >1 candidate target exceeds threshold, store resolution_status=UNRESOLVED with the candidate list in normalized_data and no link_url — surfaced in the scan summary for human disambiguation (future: per-item approve, like CAML propose).
  • Visibility: mentions inherit corpus visibility; set the analysis FK for provenance/cleanup but not created_by_analysis (which would hide them from corpus readers).
  • Service-layer compliance: extractor/resolver/writer are services; tools and services reach models through the enrichment/annotations service layer — no inline Tier-0 (visible_to_user/user_can) fusions. CorpusReference access goes through a CorpusReferenceService.

docs.title: 8. Scope & sequencing
docs.text:
In scope (v1): 1. CorpusReference model + migration + CorpusReferenceService + read-only GraphQL type/resolver. 2. ReferenceExtractor (law + internal-section + doc/exhibit) with table-driven unit tests. 3. ReferenceResolver + EnrichmentWriter with integration tests (permissioning + idempotency). 4. scan_corpus_references + apply_corpus_reference_enrichment tools + registration. 5. Proof on corpus 19 (§10).

Behind a flag / capped (v1): defined-term extraction (precision risk; default off or capped count).

Out of scope (v1): - Full frontend panel for browsing CorpusReferences (read-only GraphQL only — enough to query/verify). OC_URL links + Relationships already render, so the proof is visible without new frontend. - Actual cross-corpus linking (the model anticipates it via target_corpus + canonical_key; wiring is a later initiative). - CorpusAction/batch wrapper (design leaves the seam; not built in v1). - Pure-embedding latent-similarity links (only explicit references in v1).

docs.title: 9. Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• B — LLM-driven crawl (agent reads every section, LLM extracts/resolves via tools): flexible and catches fuzzy semantics, but at 130 docs it is expensive, non-deterministic, hard to prove, and risks hallucinated targets. Rejected as the core; the LLM is retained as orchestrator/validator only.
  • C — pure embedding-similarity graph: links sections by cosine similarity. Finds latent themes but misses the explicit references that are the actual ask and cannot normalize citations. Rejected for v1 (possible later layer).
  • Substrate — reuse-only (no new model): fastest, zero schema risk, but the cross-corpus "connection" is only a query convention over annotation.data, never a first-class record. Rejected in favor of the layered approach (reuse + small CorpusReference model) per the stated cross-corpus future.
  • Substrate — new model as the sole store (annotations only mark spans): cleanest graph but more upfront work and duplicates what Relationship already does within-document. Rejected; we let Relationship keep its job.

docs.title: 10. Testing & proof
docs.text:
• Unit — ReferenceExtractor: table-driven grammar tests, e.g. "Section 145 of the Delaware General Corporation Law" → LAW/dgcl:145; "Section 4(a)(2) of the Securities Act" → securities-act:4(a)(2); Exhibit 10.1 → DOCUMENT candidate; See "Risk Factors" → SECTION candidate.
  • Unit — ReferenceResolver: exhibit-number→document-title match; heading→OC_SECTION (and heading-text fallback when index absent); canonical-key normalization.
  • Integration — EnrichmentWriter: creates correct annotations/ relationships/CorpusReferences with correct permissioning; idempotent re-run creates zero duplicates.
  • Tool-level: scan returns an inventory and writes nothing; apply is approval-gated and transactional.
  • Proof script (docs/test_scripts/corpus_reference_enrichment.md): run scan then apply on corpus 19; assert
  • N OC_REF_LAW mentions with canonical_key including dgcl:145, dgcl:203, securities-act:4(a)(2);
  • M internal-section Relationships;
  • K doc mentions with site-relative link_url; then verify in the viewer (links clickable & route in-app; relationships render) and via GraphQL (CorpusReference rows queryable by canonical_key).

docs.title: 11. Constraints from project rules
docs.text:
• No commits/pushes for this work session — local branch only (feature/corpus-reference-enrichment).
  • Pre-commit (black/isort/flake8) + yarn lint discipline before any eventual commit; E001 service-layer check must stay green.
  • No magic numbers (use constants files); no dead code (extend/replace existing EXHIBIT_REFERENCE handling rather than duplicating).
  • Changelog: add a changelog.d/<slug>.added.md fragment (not a direct CHANGELOG.md edit) when the work lands.

docs.title: 12. Key file touch-points (anticipated)

  • opencontractserver/annotations/migrations/ — new migration.
  • opencontractserver/enrichment/ — new package: extractor.py, resolver.py, writer.py, services.py, constants.py.
  • opencontractserver/llms/tools/core_tools/corpus_references.py — two tools.
  • opencontractserver/llms/tools/tool_registry.py — registration.
