docs.title: Open-Vocabulary Authority Discovery & Recursive Graph Enrichment — Design
Open-Vocabulary Authority Discovery & Recursive Graph Enrichment — Design
docs.text: Status: draft for review (2026-06-14). Successor design to the reference enrichment engine (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-09-corpus-reference-enrichment-agent-design.md). Builds directly on the shipped engine in opencontractserver/enrichment/.

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
The shipped enrichment engine is closed-vocabulary. ReferenceExtractor (opencontractserver/enrichment/extractor.py) only fires on authorities whose alias is in a registry: the static AUTHORITY_PREFIX map (constants.py:35 — seven bodies of law: DGCL, Securities Act, Exchange Act, IRC, ICA, IAA, plus bare SEC rules) merged with aliases that bootstrapped authority corpora stamp into Document.custom_meta.authority_aliases (authorities.py:authority_alias_registry).

The consequence for less-common legal regimes is structural, not incidental:

  • A citation to an authority we have no registered alias for is never detected. "Texas Business Organizations Code § 21.401", "40 C.F.R. § 261.4", "San Francisco Police Code art. 38", "the Bank Holding Company Act" — all invisible. wanted_authorities() ranks the EXTERNAL refs the extractor did emit; it cannot surface an authority the extractor never recognized.
  • There is no external ingestion. Authorities are hand-seeded JSON (demo/authority_seeds/*.json) materialized through bootstrap_authority_corpus. Locating and importing a new body of law is a manual, code-and-curate task.

So "as we traverse our graph and enrich, find the weird ones — authorities we don't know exist a priori, and don't know where to find" is blocked at the detection layer, long before location or ingestion. It also conflates two distinct problems and adds a third opportunity:

  • A — Discovery (open-vocabulary detection): recognize that a span is a citation to some authority, even one with no registered alias. A recall problem the registry regex cannot solve.
  • B — Location & ingestion (unknown source): given a recognized-but- unknown authority, find where its text lives and import it — without a hardcoded per-source integration.
  • C — Recursion (the graph is the crawler): every authority we ingest contains its own citations (statutes cross-reference; regulations cite enabling statutes; cases cite statutes). wanted_authorities is really a frontier, and enrichment is a bounded breadth-first crawl over legal-authority space.

docs.title: 2. Goals & non-goals
docs.text:
Goals

  1. Detect citations to authorities outside the registry (federal, state, local, administrative, obscure agencies), classified by jurisdiction and authority type, with calibrated confidence.
  2. Triage detected-but-unhosted authorities into a ranked frontier.
  3. Route each frontier item to a pluggable source provider — public-domain government sources, plus an agentic web-locate fallback for the truly unknown.
  4. Gate every agentic / low-confidence ingest behind verification + a license check; never silently drop an authority we couldn't compliantly fetch — make it a visible terminal state with its candidate sources attached.
  5. Expand the frontier recursively as ingested authorities reveal their own citations, under explicit depth / budget / demand bounds.
  6. Reuse the shipped ingestion + relink machinery (bootstrap_authority_corpus, relink_corpora_for_keys) verbatim — the new work is detection, routing, and recursion, not re-plumbing persistence.

Non-goals (deliberately deferred)

  • Full case-law citation graphs. Case law (reporters, parallel cites, pincites, subsequent history) is a different modeling problem. CourtListenerProvider is stubbed behind a feature flag, off by default.
  • Authority versioning / re-pointing. The known stale-RESOLVED-reference gap (docs/architecture/reference-web-versioning.md) is out of scope; this design must not widen it. New ingests use the existing version-up path and inherit its current semantics.
  • Definition-to-usage linking for defined terms — unchanged from today.
  • Replacing Tier-1 detection. The registry path stays the trusted fast path; open-vocabulary detection is strictly additive and opt-in.

docs.title: 3. Architecture overview
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
   document text  ─────▶ │  DETECTION  (extractor, layered)          │
                         │   Tier 1  registry grammars   (trusted)   │
                         │   Tier 2a generic shape grammars (cheap)  │
                         │   Tier 2b LLM extraction pass   (recall)  │
                         │   → reconcile / dedupe / confidence       │
                         └───────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                         │ Candidates (+ jurisdiction,
                                         │              authority_type)
                                         ▼
                         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
   resolver + writer ──▶ │  PERSIST   CorpusReference (EXTERNAL)     │
   (unchanged shape)     │            + AuthorityNamespace upsert    │
                         └───────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                         ▼
                         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                         │  FRONTIER  AuthorityFrontier (the queue)  │
                         │   rank = demand × confidence − depth      │
                         └───────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                         ▼
                         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                         │  ROUTE     provider registry              │
                         │   USCode · CFR · FedRegister · StateCode  │
                         │   · CourtListener(off) · AgenticWeb(*)    │
                         └───────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                         ▼
                         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                         │  GATE      verify(citation,text) + license│
                         │   pass+trusted → ingest                   │
                         │   else → BLOCKED_LICENSE / UNLOCATED /    │
                         │          PENDING_APPROVAL  (all visible)  │
                         └───────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                         ▼  AuthoritySection[]
                         ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐
                         │  INGEST    bootstrap_authority_corpus()   │  ← REUSED
                         │            → relink_corpora_for_keys()    │  ← REUSED
                         │            → re-extract new authority doc │
                         └───────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                                         │ new outbound citations
                                         └──────────────▶ back to FRONTIER (bounded BFS)

The orchestration loop (Component 6) is the only genuinely new control flow. Everything below the GATE already exists.

docs.title: 4. Component 1 — Jurisdiction taxonomy + canonical identifiers
docs.text: Today canonical_key is a flat prefix:citation string (dgcl:145, securities-act:4(a)(2), sec-rule:506(b), term:company) and jurisdiction is implicit in the prefix. To key authorities we have never seen, add two classification dimensions and a queryable namespace table — without breaking existing keys (they remain valid and become rows in the new table).

docs.title: 4.1 Two new classification fields
docs.text:
• jurisdiction — a hierarchical, dotless code: us-federal, us-de, us-tx, us-ca, us-ca-san-francisco, us-guam. Hierarchy is by - prefix (us-ca is an ancestor of us-ca-san-francisco), enabling "all California authorities" rollups without a join table.
  • authority_type — controlled vocabulary: statute | regulation | admin-rule | municipal-ordinance | case | constitution | court-rule | guidance | treaty.

These are added to CorpusReference (indexed, nullable for back-compat) and are the routing keys providers claim on — not the opaque canonical_key prefix, which providers must never parse.

docs.title: 4.2 AuthorityNamespace (the body-of-law / routing unit)
docs.text:
One row per body of law, generalizing today's scattered alias storage into a single queryable table:

field purpose prefix (unique) canonical_key prefix, e.g. tx-boc, cfr-40, exchange-act display_name "Texas Business Organizations Code" jurisdiction / authority_type classification (Component 1.1) aliases (JSON) surface forms seen in text; feeds the extractor registry provider provider id that handles this namespace (once known) source_root_url / license where the body of law lives; its license discovery_state UNKNOWN → LOCATABLE → LOCATED → INGESTED / UNLOCATED / BLOCKED_LICENSE candidate_sources (JSON) located URLs + detected license + reject reason

authority_alias_registry(user) (authorities.py:59) is refactored to read aliases from AuthorityNamespace (visibility-scoped: a namespace contributes aliases only if its authority corpus is visible, or it is a global/public namespace) and keep reading Document.custom_meta.authority_aliases as a sync source during migration. The static AUTHORITY_PREFIX dict seeds the table once via data migration; the dict stays as the bootstrap fallback so the engine is importable without DB access (tests, cold start).

docs.title: 4.3 Key equivalence (closes the USC↔act-section gap)
docs.text: A statute is cited two ways that must dedupe to one authority: "Securities Exchange Act Section 10(b)" (exchange-act:10(b)) and "15 U.S.C. § 78j(b)" (usc-15:78j(b)) are the same law. A small AuthorityKeyEquivalence(key_a, key_b, source) table records these; a canonicalization helper picks a primary. The USCodeProvider (Component 4) populates equivalences from USLM identifiers, which is exactly the fix the versioning note already recommended ("the USLM identifiers also solve the USC→act-section mapping gap", reference-web-versioning.md:62). Equivalence is consulted in find_authority_target and the frontier dedupe so the two surface forms resolve to one ingested document.

docs.title: 5. Component 2 — Open-vocabulary detection
docs.text: Layered extraction. Each layer emits the existing Candidate dataclass (extractor.py:18), extended with optional jurisdiction, authority_type, and detection_tier / detection_confidence. Reconciliation merges layers before resolution.

docs.title: 5.1 Tier 1 — registry grammars (unchanged)
docs.text: The shipped ReferenceExtractor grammars, verbatim. Highest precision, confidence = 1.0, detection_tier = "registry". Zero behavior change when Tier 2 is off — protects every existing test and corpus.

docs.title: 5.2 Tier 2a — generic citation-shape grammars (deterministic)
docs.text:
Shape-based regexes that match citation form without knowing the body of law. New module enrichment/grammars.py. Each emits a provisional canonical_key, a minted/looked-up prefix, and jurisdiction/type guesses:

form example provisional key jurisdiction / type US Code 15 U.S.C. § 78j(b) usc-15:78j(b) us-federal / statute CFR 40 C.F.R. § 261.4 cfr-40:261.4 us-federal / regulation Fed. Register 88 Fed. Reg. 1722 fedreg:88.1722 us-federal / admin-rule Public Law Pub. L. No. 117-58 publ:117-58 us-federal / statute Statutes at Large 135 Stat. 429 stat:135.429 us-federal / statute State code (named) Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code § 21.401 tx-boc:21.401 us-tx / statute State rev. stat. Cal. Corp. Code § 300 ca-corp:300 us-ca / statute Municipal S.F. Police Code art. 38 sf-police:38 us-ca-san-francisco / municipal-ordinance Bare Act the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956 act:bank-holding-company-1956 us-federal? / statute

State/municipal forms lean on a curated abbreviation table (public Bluebook-style jurisdiction + reporter/code abbreviations — facts, not protected expression) mapping Tex. Bus. Orgs. Code → (tx-boc, us-tx, statute). The table is data, extensible without code change, seeded from public jurisdiction/abbreviation tables. confidence ≈ 0.9 for structured numeric cites, lower for bare Acts (no section ⇒ a whole-body authority, marked section = None).

docs.title: 5.3 Tier 2b — LLM extraction pass (recall)
docs.text:
A structured-output LLM pass over chunked document text catches prose and obscure references the grammars miss ("the Commission's rules under the Investment Advisers Act", "the Guam Administrative Adjudication Law"). Reuses the existing LLM framework (opencontractserver/llms/), a pydantic-ai agent created with instructions= not system_prompt= (project pitfall #14 / memory) returning, per span: {raw_text, char_span, jurisdiction, authority_type, normalized_citation, confidence}.

Controls (precision is the risk):

  • Off by default; enabled per run via the discovery tool / CorpusAction config.
  • Results below a confidence floor go to a review bucket (persisted with a needs_review flag), never auto-promoted to mentions.
  • The model is given only the document text, never told "find citations to X" (no leading), and every returned span is verified to exist at the claimed offsets before persistence (reject hallucinated spans).
  • detection_tier = "llm", confidence as returned, dampened by a calibration factor.

docs.title: 5.4 Reconciliation
docs.text: A reconcile(candidates) step (new, in the service): group by span overlap; on overlap keep the highest-precedence layer (registry > grammar > llm) and take the max confidence; dedupe identical (canonical_key, span) pairs; apply key equivalence (Component 4.3) so exchange-act:10(b) and usc-15:78j(b) collapse. Output feeds the existing ReferenceResolver unchanged — law candidates still resolve to STATUS_EXTERNAL stubs; the new classification rides along in normalized_data and the new columns.

docs.title: 6. Component 3 — The frontier
docs.text: Generalize wanted_authorities() (corpus_reference_service.py:29) from a computed aggregate into a durable, rankable queue.

docs.title: 6.1 AuthorityFrontier model (one row per wanted section key)
docs.text:
field purpose canonical_key (indexed) e.g. tx-boc:21.401 (section granularity, matching the bootstrapper's one-doc-per-section unit) namespace (FK → AuthorityNamespace) routing / body-of-law jurisdiction / authority_type denormalized for cheap filtering mention_count / key_count / corpus_count demand (recomputed from CorpusReference) discovery_state UNKNOWN → LOCATABLE → LOCATED → INGESTED / UNLOCATED / BLOCKED_LICENSE / PENDING_APPROVAL / FAILED depth hops from a seed (filing) corpus; 0 = directly cited confidence best detection confidence for this key provider / candidate_sources (JSON) / last_error routing + audit ingested_document (FK, null) the authority doc once materialized created_by_analysis (FK) provenance

Rank = mention_count × confidence with a depth penalty (a one-hop authority cited 80× outranks a three-hop authority cited twice). A demand floor (min mentions, configurable) keeps one-off cites out of the crawl.

The frontier is corpus-scoped for queries (for_corpus) but rows are keyed by canonical_key so the same authority wanted by many corpora is one ingest target — the cross-corpus dedupe the canonical_key index already anticipates. wanted_authorities() becomes a thin read over this table (back-compatible shape) plus a recompute method invoked at end of each enrichment apply.

docs.title: 7. Component 4 — Authority source providers
docs.text: A registry mirroring the shipped pluggable-pipeline pattern (PipelineComponentBase: ABC + ClassVar metadata + nested Settings dataclass + auto-discovery registry, opencontractserver/pipeline/). New package opencontractserver/enrichment/providers/.

docs.title: 7.1 BaseAuthoritySourceProvider
docs.text:
class BaseAuthoritySourceProvider(ABC):
    title: str
    description: str
    jurisdictions: ClassVar[list[str]]      # claim hints, e.g. ["us-federal"]
    authority_types: ClassVar[list[str]]    # e.g. ["statute"]
    license: ClassVar[str]                  # "public-domain", "us-gov", ...
    trust: ClassVar[int]                    # tie-break rank; official > aggregator
    class Settings: ...                     # API keys/URLs via PipelineSetting

    @abstractmethod
    def can_handle(self, item: FrontierItem) -> float: ...      # 0..1 claim
    @abstractmethod
    def locate(self, item: FrontierItem) -> SourceLocation | None: ...
    @abstractmethod
    def fetch(self, loc: SourceLocation) -> AuthorityFetchResult: ...

FrontierItem is the in-memory view of an AuthorityFrontier row (Component 6.1) — canonical_key, namespace, jurisdiction, authority_type, demand.

AuthorityFetchResult carries sections: list[AuthoritySection] (the exact shape bootstrap_authority_corpus already consumes — authorities.py:40), plus source_url, license, retrieved_at. Provider selection: highest can_handle, ties broken by trust. locate/fetch are separated so the frontier can show LOCATED (URL found) distinctly from INGESTED, and so a located-but-license-blocked source is recorded without fetching full text.

docs.title: 7.2 Concrete providers (public-domain only, per licensing decision)
docs.text:
provider source covers license USCodeProvider OLRC USLM XML bulk (uscode.house.gov) US Code titles; emits USLM ids → key equivalence public domain CFRProvider eCFR REST API (ecfr.gov) Code of Federal Regulations, all titles/agencies public domain FederalRegisterProvider federalregister.gov API rules / notices by FR citation public domain StateCodeProvider Open States bulk + official legislature sites state statutes (pluggable per state; seed high-demand states) varies — see §9 CourtListenerProvider CourtListener API (off by default) opinions public domain (opinions) AgenticWebLocatorProvider LLM + web search + fetch anything no structured provider claims per-source, gated

Structured providers convert their native format (USLM XML, eCFR JSON) into AuthoritySection lists and hand off to the existing bootstrap_authority_corpus — they add no persistence code. eCFR and OLRC are exactly the sources the versioning note already endorsed (reference-web-versioning.md:60).

docs.title: 7.3 AgenticWebLocatorProvider — the "don't know where to find it" path
docs.text: Lowest can_handle (claims only what nothing else does). An agent with web-search + URL-fetch tools, given only the normalized citation + jurisdiction/type (never the citing document's text — see §10 privacy), locates candidate sources and extracts the section text. It does not ingest; it returns candidates to the gate (Component 5). This is what lets the system reach state, municipal, tribal, territorial, and obscure-agency law without a hand-built integration per source.

docs.title: 8. Component 5 — Verify + license gate
docs.text:
Every agentic / low-confidence / non-allowlisted result passes the gate before ingest. Structured-provider results from allowlisted domains may skip straight to ingest when confidence is high.

Checks

  1. Citation match — the fetched text's own heading/identifier matches the requested canonical_key (e.g. the page's USLM id or heading is §21.401). Deterministic where possible; LLM-assisted for prose.
  2. Source trust — domain on the public-domain government allowlist (§9).
  3. License — declared/detected license is in the allowed set.
  4. Sanity — non-empty, length within bounds, parses as the claimed type.

Outcomes (all non-silent)

  • Pass + trusted + confident → ingest via bootstrap_authority_corpus; frontier → INGESTED.
  • BLOCKED_LICENSE — source(s) found but none clear the allowlist. The item stays in the frontier and governance graph as a visible node with a distinct state; candidate_sources records each URL, its detected license, and the reject reason; routes to the human-approval queue. A human may supply a compliant source or override case-by-case (override logged with who/when/why and stamps the non-PD license into the doc's custom_meta). Public-domain is the default, not a hard wall.
  • UNLOCATED — no source found at all. Visible terminal state, retryable.
  • PENDING_APPROVAL — passed checks but below the auto-ingest confidence threshold; awaits human confirm.

The crawl orchestration logs every blocked/unlocated authority (no silent truncation — project rule) and the per-run Analysis summary reports counts: {ingested, blocked_license, unlocated, pending_approval, failed}.

docs.title: 9. Licensing posture (cross-cutting)
docs.text:
Default: public-domain government primary sources only. Allowlist (domains + license tags) lives in enrichment/licensing.py:

  • Allowed: uscode.house.gov (OLRC/USLM), ecfr.gov, federalregister.gov, govinfo.gov, official *.gov state legislature/agency domains, courtlistener.com (opinions only). License tags: public-domain, us-gov-work, edict-of-government.
  • Excluded by default: Cornell LII (CC BY-NC-SA — non-commercial; project memory already flags this), commercial aggregators, anything without a clear public-domain/edict basis.

State & municipal nuance (called out, not hand-waved): the text of the law is public domain / an edict of government (cf. Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, 2020), but some official compilers (Municode, American Legal Publishing) assert copyright over their compilation/annotations. The gate distinguishes the public-domain statutory text from protected editorial matter; when only a protected-compilation source exists, the item goes BLOCKED_LICENSE with the source recorded — surfaced, never dropped. Every ingested authority doc stores license, source_url, retrieved_at in custom_meta (extends the existing stamp in authorities.py:_stamp_key).

docs.title: 10. Component 6 — Recursive frontier expansion (the crawl)
docs.text:
A bounded BFS Celery orchestration tying the pieces together. New task module enrichment/crawl.py, dispatched like the existing enrichment analyzer (ENRICHMENT_ANALYZER_TASK) and installable as a CorpusAction so the graph keeps growing as documents are added (mirrors the shipped add_document action).

seed:   open-vocab enrichment on corpus → recompute frontier (depth 0)
loop until (frontier empty | depth ≥ MAX_DEPTH | budget exhausted
            | no item ≥ DEMAND_FLOOR):
    item     = frontier.pop_top()                 # rank, demand floor
    provider = registry.select(item)              # may be AgenticWeb
    located  = provider.locate(item)              # → LOCATED | UNLOCATED
    result   = provider.fetch(located)
    if gate.verify(result, item):                 # §8
        bootstrap_authority_corpus(result.sections, …)   # REUSED → auto-relink
        re_extract(new_authority_docs)            # surfaces THEIR citations
        frontier.add(new_citations, depth = item.depth + 1)   # expansion
        item.state = INGESTED
    else:
        item.state ∈ {BLOCKED_LICENSE, UNLOCATED, PENDING_APPROVAL}  # visible
    log(item.state); analysis.tally(item.state)

Bounds (all configurable; all surfaced in the run summary):

  • MAX_DEPTH — hops from the seed corpus (default 2). Depth 0 = directly cited; depth 1 = cited by an ingested authority; etc.
  • Token/$ budget — the orchestration is budget-aware; agentic locate and Tier-2b LLM calls draw it down; the loop stops cleanly when exhausted.
  • Demand floor — skip authorities below N mentions (don't chase one-offs).
  • Per-jurisdiction caps — bound a single crawl from exploding into, say, all 50 state codes at once.

bootstrap_authority_corpus already (a) version-ups idempotently and (b) calls relink_corpora_for_keys to upgrade EXTERNAL→RESOLVED across every citing corpus. So each successful ingest automatically lights up the new authority across the whole reference web; the crawl only adds the recursion and the bounds. Re-running a crawl is idempotent: already-INGESTED keys are skipped, new mentions found in newly-ingested authority text extend the frontier.

docs.title: 11. Data-model changes (summary)
docs.text:
All additive; migrations are back-compatible.

  • CorpusReference (annotations/models.py:1901): add indexed jurisdiction, authority_type, detection_tier, detection_confidence. The _require_type_label_agreement save guard and idempotency constraints are untouched.
  • AuthorityNamespace — new (Component 4.2). Data migration seeds it from AUTHORITY_PREFIX + existing authority-corpus aliases.
  • AuthorityKeyEquivalence — new (Component 4.3).
  • AuthorityFrontier — new (Component 6.1).
  • Provider config rides the existing PipelineSettings singleton (secrets via PipelineSetting env vars), no new settings table.

docs.title: 12. Surfaces
docs.text:
Agent tools (llms/tools/core_tools/corpus_references.py, async twins as today), each with corpus_id/creator_id injected and hidden from the LLM:

  • discover_authorities(corpus_id, *, tiers=["registry","grammar"], llm=False) — scan with open-vocabulary detection on; read-only inventory of newly detectable authorities by jurisdiction/type. Extends scan_corpus_references.
  • list_authority_frontier(corpus_id) — the ranked frontier with discovery_state (supersedes / wraps list_wanted_authorities).
  • locate_authority(canonical_key) — run providers' locate for one key, return candidate sources (no ingest).
  • crawl_authorities(corpus_id, *, max_depth, budget, demand_floor) — approval-gated; runs Component 6. Returns the {ingested, blocked_license, unlocated, …} tally.

GraphQL — extend WantedAuthorityType with jurisdiction, authority_type, discovery_state; add a frontier query. All resolvers go through the service layer (CorpusReferenceService / a new AuthorityFrontierService) — no inline Tier-0 permission calls in config/graphql/ (project invariant E001).

Governance graph (governance_graph_service.py) — node payloads gain jurisdiction + authority_type (frontend colors/shapes by regime) and ghost nodes gain discovery_state so UNKNOWN / LOCATED / BLOCKED_LICENSE authorities are visually distinct — the "weird ones" become legible at a glance. Existing node kinds (primary/exhibit/statute/external) and edge types are preserved; this is additive.

docs.title: 13. Security & permissions
docs.text:
• Visibility scoping unchanged. Frontier and namespace reads derive visibility from corpus visibility via services (the CorpusReference model). find_authority_target keeps its visible_to_user + is_current filter. Ingested public authority corpora are made public via the existing make_public path so they resolve for everyone.
  • SSRF defense on every fetch. locate/fetch and the agentic tool route through one hardened HTTP client: domain allowlist enforced after DNS resolution, private/loopback/link-local IP ranges blocked, redirects re-validated against the allowlist, response size + timeout caps, no arbitrary schemes. Lives in enrichment/net.py; unit-tested against redirect-to-internal and DNS-rebind cases.
  • Privacy of the locate path (§7.3). The agentic locator receives only the normalized citation string + jurisdiction/type — never the citing document's text. External locate is opt-in per corpus (a corpus setting / explicit tool consent), because issuing a web search derived from a private corpus reveals that the corpus cites that authority. Structured-provider fetches (citation key → public gov endpoint) are lower-risk but still gated by the same opt-in for non-public corpora.
  • Agent tool fault model unchanged: operational errors return strings to the LLM; PermissionError / ToolConfirmationRequired propagate (issue #820). crawl_authorities is requires_approval.

docs.title: 14. Testing strategy (TDD, project conventions)
docs.text:
• Grammars (Tier 2a) — a golden cross-jurisdiction citation corpus (federal USC/CFR/FedReg/PubL, ≥5 state forms, ≥2 municipal, bare Acts) with expected (canonical_key, jurisdiction, authority_type); precision/recall assertions; negative cases (prose that must not match).
  • LLM pass (Tier 2b) — mocked structured outputs; assert hallucinated-span rejection, confidence bucketing, and that instructions= is used.
  • Reconciliation — registry > grammar > llm precedence; equivalence collapse (exchange-act:10(b) ≡ usc-15:78j(b)).
  • Providers — against recorded fixtures (saved USLM XML / eCFR JSON); never hit live government APIs in CI. One contract test per provider that its output AuthoritySections satisfy bootstrap_authority_corpus.
  • Gate — must reject mismatched citation, non-allowlisted domain, non-PD license, and empty/garbage text; assert BLOCKED_LICENSE / UNLOCATED are produced and recorded (never dropped).
  • SSRF client — redirect-to-internal, private-IP, DNS-rebind blocked.
  • Crawl bounds — depth, budget, demand-floor, and per-jurisdiction caps each provably terminate the loop; blocked/unlocated authorities are logged and tallied.
  • Idempotency — re-crawl creates zero duplicate authorities/refs (rerun the shipped engine's idempotency assertions over the expanded surface).
  • Permissions — frontier/namespace reads scoped to visible corpora; private authority resolves only for authorized users (extends the shipped relink_corpora_for_keys per-corpus-visibility tests).

Per project process: backend pre-commit + targeted test subsets locally, full suite in CI; one changelog.d/<slug>.<type>.md fragment per phase.

docs.title: 15. Phasing (feature branch + per-phase tracking issues)
docs.text:
This is a multi-phase initiative → a feature branch with a PR and per-phase tracking issues (project convention), not direct-to-main. Each phase is independently shippable and valuable.

phase deliverable value 0 — Taxonomy foundation jurisdiction/authority_type on CorpusReference; AuthorityNamespace + data migration from AUTHORITY_PREFIX; authority_alias_registry reads the table de-risks everything; no behavior change 1 — Tier 2a detection generic shape grammars + abbreviation table; reconciliation; discover_authorities tool finds the weird ones (structured cites) — deterministic, cheap, highest leverage 2 — Tier 2b detection LLM extraction pass + review bucket recall for prose / obscure-agency references 3 — Frontier + structured providers AuthorityFrontier; provider registry; USCode/CFR/FedRegister providers; key equivalence auto-locate + ingest for federal/regulatory 4 — Agentic locate + gate AgenticWebLocatorProvider; verify/license gate; BLOCKED_LICENSE/UNLOCATED states; SSRF client; human-approval queue reach for unknown sources without per-source code 5 — Recursive crawl bounded BFS orchestration; CorpusAction; governance-graph regime coloring + discovery_state the self-expanding reference web

Phase 1 alone answers the core request for the large class of authorities that are cited in a recognizable form. Phases 3–5 deliver the autonomous locate-and-ingest crawl for the genuinely unknown.

docs.title: 16. Risks & open questions
docs.text:
• Tier-2b precision. LLM extraction can hallucinate citations. Mitigated by span-existence verification, confidence flooring, review bucket, off-by- default. Open: calibration factor per model; revisit after Phase 2 data.
  • Provisional-key churn. A minted key (tx-boc:21.401) that later proves wrong (bad abbreviation mapping) needs reconciliation. Mitigation: keys are provisional until a provider confirms via locate; the equivalence table absorbs corrections; abbreviation table is data, fixable without migration.
  • State-source breadth. 50 states × multiple codes is a long tail. StateCodeProvider is pluggable per state; we seed high-demand states and let AgenticWebLocatorProvider cover the rest (gated). We do not block the design on exhaustive state coverage.
  • Crawl cost. Recursive + agentic + LLM can be expensive. Hard bounds (depth/budget/demand/jurisdiction) + approval gating + per-run tallies keep it controlled and observable.
  • Open question: should depth-1+ authorities (a statute cited by a statute we ingested, but not by the user's filings) join the user's governance graph, or only the shared authority library? Proposed: ingest into the shared authority library always; surface in a corpus's graph only when that corpus (transitively at depth ≤ 1) cites it — keeps each corpus's graph relevant. ```

docs.title: Problem
docs.text: CorpusGroup (multi-corpus retrieval, shipped in #2134) has a complete backend — model, CorpusGroupService, GraphQL queries + mutations, and the search_across_corpora agent tool — but the only way to create or manage a group is Django admin, which is superuser-only. Any authenticated user should be able to manage the groups they own from the app.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Per-user CRUD over the groups a user owns (creator = me). No superuser gate, no instance-wide listing — that would break the "superuser = normal user for data" invariant pinned by CorpusGroupAuthorizationInvariantsTestCase::test_superuser_has_no_blanket_data_access.

A group's form manages: title, slug (auto-generated when blank), description, is_public, member corpora (multi-select, each READ-visible to the user), and the optional bound default_agent.

Out of scope: adding a corpus to a group inline from the corpus page (membership-here is the MVP); reassigning a group's creator.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Question Decision Entry point New un-gated "Corpus Groups" item in the avatar dropdown (NavMenu.tsx userMenuItems, next to Profile/Exports) → new top-level route /corpus-groups. GlobalSettingsPanel's grid is superuser-gated, so it is the wrong home. "My groups" scoping Server-side mine: true filter on the existing corpusGroups connection. Client-side filtering would ship other users' public groups over the wire, which is exactly what the AC guards against. Django admin Remove the CorpusGroupAdmin registration — single management surface, no dead code. Agent picker reuse Build a reusable AgentConfigurationSelect; do not rewire the ~1200-line CreateCorpusActionModal to consume it in this change (follow-up).

docs.title: Backend
docs.text:
The GraphQL layer is strawberry (migrated in 6d8f21ae0), not graphene. django-filter FilterSets are still the filtering mechanism, adapted by config/graphql/core/filtering.py::setup_filterset and applied inside config/graphql/core/relay.py::resolve_django_connection.

The corpusGroups connection today exposes only the five relay pagination arguments — no filters at all (q_corpus_groups, config/graphql/corpus_queries.py). There is no way to ask for "groups I created".

CorpusFilter (config/graphql/filters.py) already implements exactly the needed trio — mine / is_public / shared_with_me, each an opt-in BooleanFilter reading self.request.user (False is a no-op, never an inversion). Rather than copy it:

  1. Extract just that trio into an OwnershipScopeFilterMixin in config/graphql/filters.py, and have CorpusFilter inherit it. Behaviour-preserving: CorpusFilter's generated arguments stay identical. CorpusFilter.filter_queryset / order_by stay put — they reference is_personal and the score column, which CorpusGroup does not have, so subclassing CorpusFilter wholesale would break.
  2. Add CorpusGroupFilter(OwnershipScopeFilterMixin, FilterSet) for the CorpusGroup model, mirroring the minimal CorpusCategoryFilter shape.
  3. Wire it onto q_corpus_groups: declare a mine strawberry argument, include it in strip_unset, and pass filterset_class=setup_filterset(CorpusGroupFilter) + filter_args={"mine": "mine"} to resolve_django_connection. _resolve_Query_corpus_groups keeps delegating to CorpusGroupService.list_visible_groups unchanged — the type's get_queryset and the service both run before the filterset, so the filter only ever narrows an already-visibility-scoped queryset. No Tier-0 call moves inline; opencontracts.E001 stays green.
  4. Regenerate the golden SDL. A new argument changes the schema, and opencontractserver/tests/test_schema_parity.py compares argument names/types/defaults against config/graphql/schema.graphql. Regenerate per docs/development/generating-new-graphql-schema.md.

opencontractserver/corpuses/admin.py — delete the CorpusGroupAdmin class and its @admin.register(CorpusGroup) decorator.

docs.title: Contract details that constrain the client
docs.text:
• Mutation inputs are relay global IDs, decoded to raw pks server-side (_decode_pks / _decode_pk). Pickers must supply global IDs.
  • updateCorpusGroup.corpusIds replaces membership when provided — the edit form always sends the full desired set, never a delta.
  • Default-agent set/clear idiom: send defaultAgentId to bind, or clearDefaultAgent: true to unbind. Never both, never an empty string.
  • Slug: leave blank to auto-generate. An explicit slug is not de-duplicated; a collision surfaces as "A corpus group with this slug already exists."

docs.title: Frontend
docs.text:
New folder frontend/src/components/corpus_groups/ (not under /admin — this is a per-user feature):

  • graphql.ts — gql documents + TS types, mirroring admin/corpus_categories/graphql.ts (types section, then operations). GET_MY_CORPUS_GROUPS passes mine: true.
  • CorpusGroupManagement.tsx — structurally mirrors admin/corpus_categories/CorpusCategoryManagement.tsx: useQuery (cache-and-network) → ScrollableTableWrapper + Table → one shared Modal whose mode derives from editingGroup !== null → ConfirmModal for delete → react-toastify for outcomes → refetch on success. No isSuperuser gate; instead an anonymous-user branch prompting sign-in.
  • index.ts barrel.

Two new reusable widgets in frontend/src/components/widgets/selectors/ (neither exists today):

  • CorpusMultiSelect.tsx — async debounced search over GET_CORPUSES, built on the existing components/common/Select react-select wrapper with isMulti. Props: { value: CorpusOption[]; onChange(next): void; disabled?; placeholder? }. Takes already-selected options as objects (id + title) so an edit form seeds its chips from the group's existing corpora without waiting on a search — the standard async-multiselect blank-chip trap.
  • AgentConfigurationSelect.tsx — async debounced search over GET_AGENT_CONFIGURATIONS (isActive: true), single-select, clearable. Clearing is what drives clearDefaultAgent: true.

Wiring: <Route path="/corpus-groups" element={<CorpusGroupManagement />} /> in App.tsx next to the other flat user routes; a corpus-groups entry in NavMenu.tsx's userMenuItems (un-gated, shown only when signed in).

docs.title: Error handling
docs.text:
• Every mutation checks the payload ok flag in onCompleted and falls back to toast.error(payload.message); onError toasts the network/GraphQL message.
  • Delete dismisses its ConfirmModal from both onCompleted and onError (the confirmLoading prop makes the dialog caller-closed).
  • Client-side validation before submit: non-empty title; slug, when supplied, must match /^[-a-zA-Z0-9_]+$/ (Django SlugField).
  • Anonymous viewer: render a sign-in prompt rather than an empty table.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Backend: CorpusGroupFilter mine scoping (owner sees own, non-owner does not see another's public group under mine: true, anonymous gets none), plus a regression assertion that CorpusFilter's arguments are unchanged by the mixin extraction.
  • Frontend frontend/tests/CorpusGroupManagement.ct.tsx via a co-located CorpusGroupManagementTestWrapper.tsx (MockedProvider + InMemoryCache + Jotai
  • backendUserObj set in a wrapper useEffect, per the CT conventions): create, edit, delete happy paths + the empty state, plus a docScreenshot. Run with --reporter=list. JSX-component imports stay in their own import statement (Playwright CT split-import rule).

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• docs/ — a short Corpus Groups user-facing note referencing the component and service by path, with the doc screenshot.
  • changelog.d/2141.added.md.

docs.title: Event‑Impact GUI — Design Spec
docs.text:
Date: 2026‑07‑20 · Branch: feature/corpus-event-impact-analysis (local, no commits/pushes) · Status: approved shape, ready for implementation plan.

Builds a GUI over the already‑implemented event‑impact backend (see docs/architecture/event-impact-analysis-gap-analysis.md §5). Backend today: CorpusEvent model, corpus-entity-extraction + event-impact-analysis task_name analyzers, EventImpactService, OC_IMPACT annotations. No GraphQL layer and no GUI exist yet — that is what this spec adds.

docs.title: Confirmed decisions (from brainstorm)
docs.text:
• Shape A — corpus‑embedded. A new "Impact" panel in Corpus Home power‑mode. Primary lens is the corpus ("what threatens this collection?").
  • Manual event creation (form with pasted text) — no URL fetch in v1.
  • Results = ranked affected‑docs list + doc highlights + per‑event summary card.
  • Readiness hint included (impact is empty on an un‑enriched corpus).
  • Run status via polling (reuse EnrichmentJobList's mechanism), not a new WS.

docs.title: 1. Backend — GraphQL layer
docs.text: All resolvers reach models through services (E001; scanned in config/graphql/). The golden SDL (config/graphql/schema.graphql) is regenerated; the parity test (test_schema_parity.py) is expected to change and is re‑pinned deliberately.

docs.title: Type
docs.text: CorpusEventType (strawberry Node) over CorpusEvent: id, title, eventDate, eventType, sourceUrl, text, extracted (GenericScalar: {authorities:[...], entities:[...]}), created, modified, plus the standard permission annotations (myPermissions, isPublished) since CorpusEvent is a BaseOCModel with guardian tables.

docs.title: Queries
docs.text:
• corpusEvents(...) — relay connection over CorpusEvent.objects.visible_to_user(user), filterable by eventType and a title/text search. Ordered -event_date.
  • corpusEventImpact(corpusId, eventId) — the ranked impact result for one (corpus, event): a list of affected documents (docId, title, score, matched authorities/entities, semanticScore) plus a summary (documentsImpacted, dominantSignal, topAuthorities, topEntities) plus runStatus (has a run completed / is one RUNNING / never run). Read from the durable OC_IMPACT annotations (data__event_id), scoped to the caller‑visible documents.

docs.title: Mutations
docs.text:
• createCorpusEvent(title, eventDate, eventType, sourceUrl, text) → CorpusEventType. Login‑required; creator = user. (Events are global — not corpus‑scoped.)
  • deleteCorpusEvent(id) → ok. Owner/DELETE‑gated (IDOR‑opaque).
  • runEventImpact(corpusId, eventId) → { ok, analysis, message }. Dispatches the event-impact-analysis analyzer (creates an Analysis, analyze_event first if extracted is null, then .delay() the task). Mirrors runCorpusEnrichment. Corpus UPDATE‑gated (it writes OC_IMPACT annotations to the corpus) and the event must be visible to the caller.

docs.title: Service layer
docs.text:
• New CorpusEventService (opencontractserver/enrichment/services/) — list_visible(user, ...), get_or_none(user, event_id), create(user, ...), delete(user, event_id), and get_impact(user, corpus, event) (reads OC_IMPACT annotations on MIN‑visible docs → ranked rows + summary). Keeps all Tier‑0 (visible_to_user/user_can) out of resolvers (E001).
  • EventImpactService.run_impact already exists; the runEventImpact resolver validates + dispatches, the task calls the service (as built).

docs.title: 2. Permissions & security (explicit)
docs.text:
Modeled on runCorpusEnrichment (config/graphql/enrichment_mutations.py) and the CLAUDE.md security patterns. Every resolver passes request=info.context so the Tier‑2 permission cache engages.

Operation Gate Notes corpusEvents (list) CorpusEvent.objects.visible_to_user(user) own + public; no cross‑user leak createCorpusEvent authenticated (@login_required) creator = user; events are global deleteCorpusEvent event.user_can(user, DELETE, request=…) owner/guardian; IDOR‑opaque error runEventImpact corpus UPDATE + event READ writes annotations → editor‑gated corpusEventImpact (results) corpus READ + MIN(corpus, doc) results only over caller‑visible docs

Rules, concretely: 1. Global‑ID type validation. from_global_id on corpusId/eventId; reject if the type prefix isn't CorpusType/CorpusEventType (never let a wrong‑type pk flow downstream — the enrichment mutation's IDOR guard). 2. IDOR‑opaque errors. For a corpus/event the caller can't see, return the SAME "Resource not found or you do not have permission." whether it's missing or hidden — no existence oracle. CorpusService.get_or_none(...) / CorpusEventService.get_or_none(...) return None for both. 3. Run gate. runEventImpact requires the caller can UPDATE the corpus (writes OC_IMPACT rows), checked via CorpusService/user_can(..., request=info.context) BEFORE dispatch. The event must be visible (READ). 4. Results never leak private docs. get_impact scopes to CorpusDocumentService.get_corpus_documents_visible_to_user — a caller with corpus READ but not per‑document READ never sees impact on a private document (the MIN(corpus, document) rule the impact analyzer already enforces at run time). 5. XSS. CorpusEvent.text/extracted are user content rendered in the panel — escape on the frontend (the panel shows event text + matched keys); documented at the resolver.

docs.title: 3. Frontend — the Impact panel
docs.text:
New power‑mode sidebar item "Impact" → CorpusImpactPanel.tsx (frontend/src/components/corpuses/CorpusHome/impact/). Registered alongside the existing panels (Analyses, Research, …).

Panel layout, top → bottom: 1. Readiness hint — a compact line: "This corpus has N law references and M entities." If either is 0, a nudge + link to run reference enrichment / entity extraction (they gate the authority/entity signals). Data from a lightweight count (reuse the intelligence‑panel reference/entity counts). 2. Event selector + creator — a searchable list of the user's visible events to pick one; a "New event" button opens an inline form: title, event_date (date picker), event_type (select: news/legislation/regulation/other), source_url (optional), and a text area for the article/bill/rule body. Submit → createCorpusEvent → the new event becomes selected. 3. "Assess this corpus" button → runEventImpact(corpusId, eventId) → in‑progress state (poll the returned Analysis status, reuse the EnrichmentJobList polling; disable the button while RUNNING). 4. Results (once a run for this (corpus, event) has completed): - Summary card: documents impacted · dominant signal · top matched authorities/entities · event date + type. - Ranked affected‑docs list: each row = document title · score · signal badges (⚖️ authority / 🏷️ entity / ≈ semantic) · the matched canonical keys. Click a row → navigate to the document (deep link the app already supports); the OC_IMPACT annotation highlights the exposure locus (renders today, no new viewer work).

docs.title: Reuse (DRY)
docs.text:
• EnrichmentRunner / EnrichmentJobList (components/admin/enrichment/) — the run‑button + status‑polling + result‑list shape.
  • The power‑mode panel registration + sidebar (CorpusHome power‑user layout).
  • Corpus doc‑card / list styling + existing badge components.
  • Existing annotation highlighting in the document viewer (impact = an annotation, so it's already rendered).

docs.title: 4. Data flow
docs.text:
open corpus → power mode → "Impact" panel
  → GraphQL: corpusEvents (list) + corpusEventImpact (existing results, if any)
  → pick or create (createCorpusEvent) an event
  → "Assess this corpus" → runEventImpact → Analysis(status=CREATED) + task.delay()
  → poll Analysis.status (RUNNING → COMPLETED)
  → corpusEventImpact → summary card + ranked list
  → click a doc → open it → OC_IMPACT highlights the exposure

docs.title: 5. Scope
docs.text:
In v1: - GraphQL: CorpusEventType, corpusEvents, corpusEventImpact, createCorpusEvent, deleteCorpusEvent, runEventImpact; regenerated SDL. - CorpusEventService; results via OC_IMPACT annotations. - CorpusImpactPanel with readiness hint, event pick/create form, Assess + polling, summary card + ranked list + click‑through. - Backend tests (resolvers + service + permission/IDOR tests). - Frontend component test (CT) through a test wrapper + a doc screenshot.

Deferred: URL‑fetch events; global event library / cross‑corpus rollup (shape B/C); entity‑alias resolution; automated event feeds; event editing (create + delete only in v1).

docs.title: 6. Testing plan
docs.text:
• Backend: service unit tests (list_visible filtering, get_impact shaping); resolver tests incl. permission matrix — non‑owner can't delete; a corpus‑READ‑but‑not‑UPDATE user can't runEventImpact; a hidden corpus/event yields the opaque error; results exclude a private document for a corpus‑READ‑only caller (MIN visibility). Schema‑parity regenerated.
  • Frontend: a CorpusImpactPanel CT mounted through a test wrapper (MockedProvider + Jotai), asserting: create‑event form posts, Assess dispatches, a completed run renders the summary card + ranked list. Doc screenshot impact--corpus-panel--with-results via docScreenshot.

docs.title: 7. Risks / notes
docs.text:
• Golden‑SDL parity test changes — regenerate deliberately (command in the test docstring).
  • E001 system check — all new resolvers must route through services.
  • Run‑status polling: match whatever EnrichmentJobList does (avoid a bespoke mechanism).
  • Local only — no commits/pushes.

docs.title: Backend Telemetry
docs.text: OpenContracts backend uses PostHog to collect anonymous usage telemetry. This data helps guide development priorities by understanding how the platform is used.

docs.title: What We Collect
docs.text: Backend telemetry records the following events:

docs.title: Periodic Events
docs.text:
Event Description Frequency Properties usage_heartbeat Aggregate usage statistics Daily See below

The usage_heartbeat event includes: - user_count — Active users - document_count — Non-deleted documents - corpus_count — Total corpuses - annotation_count — User annotations (excludes structural) - conversation_count — Active conversations/threads - message_count — Active messages - version — OpenContracts version - installation_age_days — Days since installation

docs.title: Real-time Events
docs.text:
Event Description Properties user_created A new user account is created user_count (total users) document_uploaded A document is uploaded user_id, env

All events include: - installation_id — Unique anonymous identifier for your installation - timestamp — When the event occurred - package — Always opencontracts

docs.title: What We Do NOT Collect
docs.text:
• Document contents or filenames
  • User identities, emails, or personal information
  • Extracted data or annotations
  • Query contents or search terms
  • IP addresses or location data

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Backend telemetry is controlled by environment variables in your Django settings:

Variable Default Description TELEMETRY_ENABLED True Master switch for backend telemetry POSTHOG_API_KEY (set) PostHog project API key POSTHOG_HOST https://us.i.posthog.com PostHog API endpoint

docs.title: Disabling Telemetry
docs.text:
To disable backend telemetry, set the environment variable:

TELEMETRY_ENABLED=False

Or in your .env file:

TELEMETRY_ENABLED=False

When disabled, no events are sent to PostHog and no data leaves your server.

docs.title: Technical Details
docs.text:
• Location: config/telemetry.py
  • Singleton client: PostHog client is lazily initialized and reused
  • Async sending: Events are queued and sent asynchronously by a background thread
  • Graceful shutdown: An atexit handler ensures pending events are flushed on process exit
  • Test mode: Telemetry is automatically disabled when MODE=TEST

docs.title: Periodic Task Setup
docs.text:
The daily usage_heartbeat task is automatically configured when you run migrations:

python manage.py migrate

This creates a PeriodicTask entry in django-celery-beat's database scheduler. The task: - Runs daily at midnight UTC - Is only created if TELEMETRY_ENABLED=True at migration time - Can be managed via Django admin under "Periodic Tasks"

Requirements: Celery Beat must be running for periodic tasks to execute:

celery -A config.celery_app beat --loglevel=info

docs.title: Implementation
docs.text:
Events are recorded via the record_event() function:

from config.telemetry import record_event

# Record an event with properties
record_event("my_event", {"property": "value"})

The function returns True if the event was queued successfully, False otherwise. It never raises exceptions to avoid disrupting normal operations.

docs.title: Frontend Analytics
docs.text: OpenContracts frontend uses PostHog for optional, consent-based analytics tracking. This helps understand how users interact with the interface to improve the experience.

docs.title: Privacy-First Design
docs.text:
Frontend analytics is designed with privacy as a priority:

  1. Consent required — Analytics only activates after explicit user consent via the cookie consent dialog
  2. Do Not Track respected — The browser's DNT setting is honored
  3. No autocapture — We don't automatically capture clicks or form submissions
  4. CI/test detection — Analytics is automatically disabled in test environments

docs.title: What We Collect
docs.text:
When enabled and consented, the frontend can track:

Event Type Description Page views Navigation between pages (manually triggered for SPA) Custom events Feature usage statistics (opt-in per feature)

docs.title: What We Do NOT Collect
docs.text:
• Document contents or extracted data
  • User credentials or personal information
  • Form inputs or search queries
  • Automatic click tracking (autocapture is disabled)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Frontend analytics is configured in frontend/public/env-config.js:

window._env_ = {
  // ... other settings ...
  REACT_APP_POSTHOG_API_KEY: "your-api-key-here",
  REACT_APP_POSTHOG_HOST: "https://us.i.posthog.com",
};
Variable Default Description REACT_APP_POSTHOG_API_KEY (empty) PostHog project API key REACT_APP_POSTHOG_HOST https://us.i.posthog.com PostHog API endpoint

docs.title: Disabling Analytics
docs.text:
To disable frontend analytics entirely, leave REACT_APP_POSTHOG_API_KEY empty or unset:

window._env_ = {
  // ... other settings ...
  REACT_APP_POSTHOG_API_KEY: "",  // Empty = disabled
  REACT_APP_POSTHOG_HOST: "https://us.i.posthog.com",
};

When disabled: - The cookie consent dialog won't mention analytics - No PostHog scripts are initialized - No data is sent to any analytics service

docs.title: User Controls
docs.text:
Even when analytics is configured, users have control:

  1. Cookie consent — Users must accept cookies to enable analytics
  2. Browser DNT — Do Not Track browser setting is respected
  3. Opt-out — Users can clear consent via browser localStorage

docs.title: Technical Details
docs.text:
• Location: frontend/src/utils/analytics.ts
  • Consent storage: localStorage key oc_analyticsConsent
  • Initialization: Lazy — only when consent is given and API key is configured

docs.title: Available Functions
docs.text:
import {
  initializePostHog,      // Initialize PostHog (called automatically on consent)
  shutdownPostHog,        // Shutdown and clear data
  hasAnalyticsConsent,    // Check if user consented
  setAnalyticsConsent,    // Set consent status
  isPostHogConfigured,    // Check if API key is set
  identifyUser,           // Associate events with user
  trackEvent,             // Track custom event
  trackPageView,          // Track page navigation
  resetAnalytics,         // Reset identity (e.g., on logout)
} from "./utils/analytics";

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
// Track a custom event
trackEvent("feature_used", { feature_name: "document_export" });

// Track a page view
trackPageView("/documents/123");

// Identify user after login
identifyUser(userId, { plan: "enterprise" });

// Reset on logout
resetAnalytics();

docs.title: Test Environment Detection
docs.text:
Analytics is automatically disabled when:

  • Running in Playwright or Cypress test environments
  • import.meta.env.MODE === "test" or import.meta.env.VITEST is set
  • Hostname includes "test" or "ci-"
  • window._env_.CI === "true"

This ensures no test data pollutes production analytics.

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Verify that anonymous users on public corpuses get multi-turn conversation, working timeline, context tracking, and context exhaustion handling.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• A public corpus exists with at least one document
  • User is NOT logged in (anonymous/incognito)

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the public corpus page (anonymous)
  2. Open the chat interface
  3. Send a message: "What is this corpus about?"
  4. Verify:
  5. Response streams back (not stuck loading)
  6. Timeline shows steps (tool calls, thoughts) — NOT "0 steps"
  7. Context meter at bottom shows > 0% after response
  8. Send a follow-up: "Can you tell me more about the first document?"
  9. Verify:
  10. Response references the prior conversation (multi-turn works)
  11. Context meter has increased
  12. Timeline shows steps for this message too
  13. Refresh the page
  14. Verify: Chat is gone (ephemeral — not persisted)

docs.title: Expected Results
docs.text:
• Multi-turn conversation works within session
  • Timeline and context tracking are accurate
  • Data is lost on refresh (by design)

docs.title: Test: Batch-run an agent corpus action across every doc in a corpus
Test: Batch-run an agent corpus action across every doc in a corpus
Purpose
docs.text:
End-to-end verification of the new startCorpusActionBatchRun GraphQL mutation + Layers-icon UI button. Confirms that:

  1. A non-superuser collaborator with corpus UPDATE can press the button.
  2. Every active document in the corpus that has not already been processed gets a CorpusActionExecution(trigger="manual_batch", status="QUEUED") row.
  3. The run_agent_corpus_action Celery task fires once per eligible doc.
  4. Pressing the button a second time skips docs that are already QUEUED | RUNNING | COMPLETED (idempotent re-press).
  5. A FAILED execution is re-queued on the next press (retry path).

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Local stack up: docker compose -f local.yml up.
  • Migrations applied through corpuses/0051_add_manual_batch_trigger.
  • An LLM API key configured on the agents.AgentConfiguration you'll use (or test against a lightweight task_instructions-only action that just exercises the dispatch path — the agent will fail to load the LLM but the execution rows + dispatch are what we're verifying here).

docs.title: 1. Create a corpus with three docs and an agent action
docs.text:
docker compose -f local.yml run --rm django python manage.py shell -c "
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from opencontractserver.corpuses.models import Corpus, CorpusAction, CorpusActionTrigger
from opencontractserver.documents.models import Document, DocumentPath
from opencontractserver.types.enums import PermissionTypes
from opencontractserver.utils.permissioning import set_permissions_for_obj_to_user

User = get_user_model()
owner = User.objects.filter(is_superuser=True).first()
collab, _ = User.objects.get_or_create(username='batch-test-collab', defaults={'email': 'c@test'})

corpus = Corpus.objects.create(title='Batch Test Corpus', creator=owner)
set_permissions_for_obj_to_user(collab, corpus, [PermissionTypes.UPDATE])

for i in range(3):
    doc = Document.objects.create(title=f'Batch Doc {i}', creator=owner)
    DocumentPath.objects.create(
        document=doc, corpus=corpus, path=f'/documents/doc_{doc.pk}',
        version_number=1, is_current=True, is_deleted=False, creator=owner,
    )

action = CorpusAction.objects.create(
    corpus=corpus,
    name='Generate Descriptions',
    trigger=CorpusActionTrigger.ADD_DOCUMENT,
    task_instructions='Read the document and update its description with a one-sentence summary.',
    creator=owner,
)
print(f'corpus={corpus.id} action={action.id} collab={collab.id}')
"
